cve_description: NULL Pointer Dereference in Homebrew mruby prior to 3.2.
cause_reason: C1 only added the `val` guard to the OP_HASHADD code path in gen_hash, but the same vulnerability existed in other branches within the same function — specifically the OP_HASH and OP_HASHCAT paths that also perform stack operations when val is false. C2 applies the same `val &&` guard pattern to those additional branches.

cve_description: CVAT is an opensource interactive video and image annotation tool for computer vision. Versions prior to 2.0.0 were found to be subject to a Server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. Validation has been added to urls used in the affected code path in version 2.0.0. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this issue.
cause_reason: C1 only applied SSRF validation to task download URLs using client-side DNS resolution checks, but missed two critical aspects: (1) it didn't protect against redirects/DNS rebinding (a TOCTOU issue requiring network-level enforcement via smokescreen proxy instead of pre-request validation), and (2) it didn't apply SSRF protection to webhook URLs at all. C2 replaced the client-side validation with a network-level proxy (smokescreen) that handles redirects, and extended protection to the webhook code path — applying the same fix pattern to an additional code scope.

cve_description: Bytecode Viewer (BCV) is a Java/Android reverse engineering suite. Versions of the package prior to 2.11.0 are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (AKA "Zip Slip"). The vulnerability is exploited using a specially crafted archive that holds directory traversal filenames (e.g. ../../evil.exe). The Zip Slip vulnerability can affect numerous archive formats, including zip, jar, tar, war, cpio, apk, rar and 7z. The attacker can then overwrite executable files and either invoke them remotely or wait for the system or user to call them, thus achieving remote command execution on the victim’s machine. The impact of a Zip Slip vulnerability would allow an attacker to create or overwrite existing files on the filesystem. In the context of a web application, a web shell could be placed within the application directory to achieve code execution. All users should upgrade to BCV v2.11.0 when possible to receive a patch. There are no recommended workarounds aside from upgrading.
cause_reason: C1's Zip Slip check compared the extracted file's canonical path against the raw (non-canonicalized) destinationDir without a trailing separator. C2 fixes this by canonicalizing destinationDir and ensuring it ends with a path separator, preventing edge cases where a path like '/tmp/evil' could pass a startsWith check against '/tmp/evi' or where non-canonical destination paths caused the check to fail.

cve_description: Eclipse Californium is a Java implementation of RFC7252 - Constrained Application Protocol for IoT Cloud services. In versions prior to 3.7.0, and 2.7.4, Californium is vulnerable to a Denial of Service. Failing handshakes don't cleanup counters for throttling, causing the threshold to be reached without being released again. This results in permanently dropping records. The issue was reported for certificate based handshakes, but may also affect PSK based handshakes. It generally affects client and server as well. This issue is patched in version 3.7.0 and 2.7.4. There are no known workarounds. main: commit 726bac57659410da463dcf404b3e79a7312ac0b9 2.7.x: commit 5648a0c27c2c2667c98419254557a14bac2b1f3f
cause_reason: C1 fixed the main branch (3.7.x) with LimitedRunnable counter cleanup and connection.shutdown() in remove paths, but C2 applies the same fix patterns to the 2.7.x branch, which has the same vulnerable code paths. C2 adds connection.isExecuting() checks to multiple run() methods and adds pending job execution during connection removal in the 2.7.x InMemoryConnectionStore - the same fix patterns C1 applied to the main branch but for the older codebase that doesn't use LimitedRunnable.

cve_description: APIs to evaluate content with Velocity is a package for APIs to evaluate content with Velocity. Starting with version 2.3 and prior to 12.6.7, 12.10.3, and 13.0, the velocity scripts are not properly sandboxed against using the Java File API to perform read or write operations on the filesystem. Writing an attacking script in Velocity requires the Script rights in XWiki so not all users can use it, and it also requires finding an XWiki API which returns a File. The problem has been patched in versions 12.6.7, 12.10.3, and 13.0. There is no easy workaround for fixing this vulnerability other than upgrading and being careful when giving Script rights.
cause_reason: C1 had a typo in the whitelist: 'getsimpleName' instead of 'getsimplename'. Since the lookup uses toLowerCase() comparison, the mixed-case entry 'getsimpleName' was stored literally but would never match properly. C2 fixes this by correcting the string to 'getsimplename' and adding a prepareSet() helper that normalizes all entries to lowercase.

cve_description: Use After Free in op_is_set_bp in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.6.
cause_reason: C1 reordered code to avoid the UAF but failed to decouple op_dst/op_src from regitem lifetime. C2 fixes this by introducing strdup() to create independent copies and adding corresponding free() calls, directly addressing the pointer lifetime mismatch where dangling pointers survived regprofile invalidation.

cve_description: Rizin is a UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset. Versions 0.4.0 and prior are vulnerable to an out-of-bounds write when getting data from Luac files. A user opening a malicious Luac file could be affected by this vulnerability, allowing an attacker to execute code on the user's machine. Commits 07b43bc8aa1ffebd9b68d60624c9610cf7e460c7 and 05bbd147caccc60162d6fba9baaaf24befa281cd contain fixes for the issue.
cause_reason: C1 allocated the upvalue_names buffer based only on rz_list_length(proto->upvalue_entries), but then iterated over proto->dbg_upvalue_entries to populate it. C2 fixes this by using RZ_MAX of both list lengths, handling the edge case where dbg_upvalue_entries is longer than upvalue_entries, which causes an OOB write.

cve_description: OpenClinica is an open source software for Electronic Data Capture (EDC) and Clinical Data Management (CDM). OpenClinica prior to version 3.16 is vulnerable to path traversal in multiple endpoints, leading to arbitrary file read/write, and potential remote code execution. There are no known workarounds. This issue has been patched and users are recommended to upgrade.
cause_reason:
Looking at the commit history, I need to understand the timeline:

**C2 (1578ee1b)** was actually the **first** patch attempt, and **C1 (6f864e86)** was the follow-up. Let me verify by examining the content:

- C2 adds `FilenameUtils.getName()` sanitization and `".."` checks as the initial fix approach
- C1 replaces/augments with canonical path validation approach

Wait, re-reading the problem statement: C1 is the incomplete fix, C2 is the follow-up that completes it. Let me re-examine.

**C1 (6f864e86):** Introduced canonical path validation (`getCanonicalPath().startsWith(baseDir)`) across multiple endpoints. In `DownloadAttachedFileServlet`, it **removed** the explicit `".."` check. In `BatchCRFMigrationController`, it replaced `FilenameUtils.getName()` with canonical path checks. In `DownloadVersionSpreadSheetServlet`, it added canonical path validation.

**C2 (1578ee1b):** This is the follow-up fix that:
1. **Re-adds** the `".."` check in `DownloadAttachedFileServlet` (defense-in-depth)
2. **Re-adds** `FilenameUtils.getName()` in `BatchCRFMigrationController` and `OpenRosaSubmissionController` 
3. **Adds** `FilenameUtils.getName()` to sanitize filenames in `DownloadVersionSpreadSheetServlet` before constructing File objects

C1's canonical path approach was correct in concept but insufficient because it didn't sanitize the file names themselves. The same sanitization pattern (`FilenameUtils.getName()` and `".."` checks) needed to be applied across all the affected endpoints. C2 applies these additional sanitization measures across multiple servlets/controllers.

This is a breadth problem — C1 applied one type of fix (canonical path validation) but didn't also apply filename sanitization (`FilenameUtils.getName()`, `".."` checks) across the affected endpoints.

cve_description: drachtio-server 0.8.18 has a request-handler.cpp event_cb use-after-free for any request.
cause_reason: C1 correctly captured *fdp into a local variable to prevent use-after-free from pointer modification, but missed the specific edge case where CURL_POLL_REMOVE triggers socket cleanup via remsock(). C2 explicitly detects the CURL_POLL_REMOVE state, defers the remsock() call to the event_cb where it can safely return early, preventing dereferencing of a freed pointer.

cve_description: This affects the package codecov before 2.0.16. The vulnerability occurs due to not sanitizing gcov arguments before being being provided to the popen method.
cause_reason: C1 correctly identified the need to sanitize gcov arguments but only stripped '&' characters while keeping shell=True. C2 completed the fix by changing shell=True to shell=False and passing commands as lists, eliminating all shell metacharacter injection vectors (;, |, $(), etc.) that C1's narrow character-class regex missed.

cve_description: mitmproxy is an interactive, SSL/TLS-capable intercepting proxy. In mitmproxy 7.0.4 and below, a malicious client or server is able to perform HTTP request smuggling attacks through mitmproxy. This means that a malicious client/server could smuggle a request/response through mitmproxy as part of another request/response's HTTP message body. While mitmproxy would only see one request, the target server would see multiple requests. A smuggled request is still captured as part of another request's body, but it does not appear in the request list and does not go through the usual mitmproxy event hooks, where users may have implemented custom access control checks or input sanitization. Unless mitmproxy is used to protect an HTTP/1 service, no action is required. The vulnerability has been fixed in mitmproxy 8.0.0 and above. There are currently no known workarounds.
cause_reason: C1 only applied header validation in the HTTP/1 layer (_http1.py) for both requests and responses, but did not apply the same validation at the shared HTTP layer level (__init__.py) where it would cover all HTTP versions (HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2). C2 moved validation to a centralized `validate` module and applied it in the common `HttpStream` class (`check_invalid`), covering all protocol versions and adding version-specific rules (e.g., rejecting Transfer-Encoding in HTTP/1.0). C2 also added stricter content-length parsing and response smuggling detection that C1 missed.

cve_description: A directory traversal vulnerability in the SevenZipFile.extractall() function of the python library py7zr v0.20.0 and earlier allows attackers to write arbitrary files via extracting a crafted 7z file.
cause_reason: C1 used resolve() for path validation which doesn't correctly handle '..' traversal sequences on all platforms (especially Windows). C2 replaces resolve() with a custom canonical_path() function that processes '..' components purely via string manipulation on PurePath objects, adds explicit absolute path rejection in check_archive_path(), and introduces is_relative_to() wrapper - all addressing specific path traversal variants that C1's resolve()-based approach failed to catch.

cve_description: A symbolic link issue was found in rpm. It occurs when rpm sets the desired permissions and credentials after installing a file. A local unprivileged user could use this flaw to exchange the original file with a symbolic link to a security-critical file and escalate their privileges on the system. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity as well as system availability.
cause_reason: C1 correctly added AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW for file opening but did not apply the same dirfd-based safe operation pattern to the metadata-setting functions (fsmChown, fsmChmod, fsmUtime, fsmSetFCaps, fsmSetmeta). C2 systematically converted all these path-based syscalls to their dirfd-based equivalents (fchownat, fchmodat, utimensat) with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW flags, applying the same fix pattern across all code scopes that needed it.

cve_description: A heap overflow vulnerability was found in bluez in versions prior to 5.63. An attacker with local network access could pass specially crafted files causing an application to halt or crash, leading to a denial of service.
cause_reason: C1's bounds check used the full PDU length including headers instead of just the payload length, making the validation overly restrictive by checking against the wrong value.

cve_description: An improper link resolution flaw can occur while extracting an archive leading to changing modes, times, access control lists, and flags of a file outside of the archive. An attacker may provide a malicious archive to a victim user, who would trigger this flaw when trying to extract the archive. A local attacker may use this flaw to gain more privileges in a system.
cause_reason: C1's fix only handled the symlink case (S_ISLNK check) when open() failed, but assumed all fixup entries were directories. C2 introduced la_verify_filetype() to explicitly validate that the on-disk file type matches the declared archive entry filetype for ALL file types (regular files, symlinks, sockets, block/char devices, FIFOs, directories), not just symlinks. C1's type verification logic was incomplete because it didn't account for all possible file type variants that could appear in the fixup list.

cve_description: swaylock before 1.6 allows attackers to trigger a crash and achieve unlocked access to a Wayland compositor.
cause_reason: C1 introduced the ext-session-lock-v1 protocol but left the 'locked' callback as a no-op ('Who cares'), never waiting for the compositor to confirm the session was locked before proceeding. This created a race condition (TOCTOU) where the lockscreen could proceed or daemonize before the session was actually secured, allowing a crash to yield unlocked access. C2 fixes this by adding a 'locked' state flag and a dispatch loop that blocks until the compositor confirms the lock.

cve_description: Moddable commit before 135aa9a4a6a9b49b60aa730ebc3bcc6247d75c45 was discovered to contain an out-of-bounds read via the function fxUint8Getter at /moddable/xs/sources/xsDataView.c.
cause_reason: C1 used `offset + delta` with a post-computation overflow check `(end < offset)`, but this signed integer overflow is undefined behavior in C and cannot reliably detect all overflow cases. C2 replaced the arithmetic with `fxAddChunkSizes()`, an overflow-safe addition function, to properly handle large values that could cause integer overflow during the addition itself. This is a depth problem where C1's fix logic was correct in intent but missed specific large value combinations that could bypass the post-hoc overflow check.

cve_description: Use After Free in GitHub repository mruby/mruby prior to 3.2.
cause_reason: C1 fixed direct pointer invalidation by using indexed access via `regs` macro, but failed to refresh the `ci` variable after VM re-entry points (e.g., calls to mrb_hash_set, mrb_ary_splat, mrb_range_new, etc.). C2 adds `ci = mrb->c->ci;` refreshes at all locations where re-entry can invalidate the cached call frame, ensuring consistent state across execution contexts.

cve_description: Yet Another UserAgent Analyzer (Yauaa) is a java library that tries to parse and analyze the useragent string and extract as many relevant attributes as possible. Applications using the Client Hints analysis feature introduced with 7.0.0 can crash because the Yauaa library throws an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. If uncaught the exception will result in a program crash. Applications that do not use this feature are not affected. Users are advised to upgrade to version 7.9.0. Users unable to upgrade may catch and discard any ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown by the Yauaa library.
cause_reason: C1 rewrote the version parsing logic but still used unsafe `split("\\.")` without bounds limits and `substring(0, indexOf('.'))` in multiple code locations. C2 applied safe splitting patterns (`DOT_SPLITTER.split(version, 2)[0]`) across all remaining locations that still had the unsafe split operations, including the Opera version extraction path and the generic brand version extraction, plus a similar fix in HostnameExtracter.

cve_description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. When `tf.raw_ops.FusedResizeAndPadConv2D` is given a large tensor shape, it overflows. We have patched the issue in GitHub commit d66e1d568275e6a2947de97dca7a102a211e01ce. The fix will be included in TensorFlow 2.11. We will also cherrypick this commit on TensorFlow 2.10.1, 2.9.3, and TensorFlow 2.8.4, as these are also affected and still in supported range.
cause_reason: C1 only fixed the `resized_shape` construction in `conv_ops_fused_image_transform.cc` by switching to `TensorShape::BuildTensorShape`, but the same integer overflow vulnerability existed in many other `ShapeFromFormat` call sites across multiple files (`conv_ops.cc`, `conv_ops_3d.cc`, `conv_ops_fused_impl.h`, `conv_ops_fused_int8.cc`, `conv_ops_using_gemm.cc`, and the `out_shape` in the same file). C2 applied the same fix pattern (`ShapeFromFormatWithStatus` with `OP_REQUIRES_OK`) to all these additional call sites.

cve_description: Nginx NJS v0.7.2 was discovered to contain a segmentation violation in the function njs_array_prototype_sort at src/njs_array.c.
cause_reason: C1 failed to account for the array's state (length, element positions) being mutated during the sort callback execution. C2 adds a length consistency check for the fast path and removes the position-change optimization in the slow path, ensuring correct behavior when the array is modified during sorting across the callback context.

cve_description: A stored cross site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in Checkmk 1.6.0x prior to 1.6.0p19 allows an authenticated remote attacker to inject arbitrary JavaScript via a javascript: URL in a view title.
cause_reason: C1 correctly refactored the href/target parsing but intentionally omitted URL scheme validation (as noted by the test comment 'This will be refused in the next step'). C2 added the missing scheme validation check to restrict unescaping to only http/https protocols, blocking javascript: and other dangerous URL schemes. This is a depth problem where the fix logic was incomplete for specific dangerous input values (javascript: URLs).

cve_description: Out-of-bounds Read in mrb_obj_is_kind_of in in GitHub repository mruby/mruby prior to 3.2. # Impact: Possible arbitrary code execution if being exploited.
cause_reason: C1 only protected the prepended/module branch by conditionally reassigning target_class from ci, but missed that the initial assignment of target_class from MRB_PROC_TARGET_CLASS(p) could itself be invalid. C2 fixes this by changing the initialization point of target_class to always use mrb_vm_ci_target_class(ci), eliminating the unsafe code path that C1 left unprotected.

cve_description: If an OpenID Connect provider supports the "none" algorithm (i.e., tokens with no signature), pac4j v5.3.0 (and prior) does not refuse it without an explicit configuration on its side or for the "idtoken" response type which is not secure and violates the OpenID Core Specification. The "none" algorithm does not require any signature verification when validating the ID tokens, which allows the attacker to bypass the token validation by injecting a malformed ID token using "none" as the value of "alg" key in the header with an empty signature value.
cause_reason: C1 correctly introduced the `allowUnsignedIdTokens` configuration flag to block unsigned tokens by default, but missed the specific condition where the response_type includes 'id_token'. Per the OpenID Connect spec, 'none' algorithm must never be accepted when id_token is returned directly from the authorization endpoint, even if the client explicitly allows unsigned tokens. C2 adds this additional response_type check within the same code block.

cve_description: global heap buffer overflow in skip_range in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 8.2.4763. This vulnerability is capable of crashing software, Bypass Protection Mechanism, Modify Memory, and possible remote execution
cause_reason: C1 immediately assigned eap->cmd to the string literal "+", causing subsequent pointer arithmetic and comparisons between eap->cmd and cmd_start to operate on unrelated memory regions (string literal vs. buffer). C2 fixes this by deferring the assignment using a use_plus_cmd flag, keeping eap->cmd pointing into the original buffer until all pointer-relative operations are complete, and also adding a break to prevent further invalid pointer-based parsing.

cve_description: A vulnerability, which was classified as problematic, was found in GPAC 2.1-DEV-rev490-g68064e101-master. Affected is the function lsr_translate_coords of the file laser/lsr_dec.c. The manipulation leads to integer overflow. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The name of the patch is b3d821c4ae9ba62b3a194d9dcb5e99f17bd56908. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue. VDB-214518 is the identifier assigned to this vulnerability.
cause_reason: C1 used s64 types with `(0x00000001UL << nb_bits)` to fix the integer overflow, but this still produces undefined behavior when nb_bits equals 31 on 32-bit platforms (shifting 1 into the sign bit). C2 reverts to s32 and explicitly handles the nb_bits==31 boundary case with the constant 0x80000000, avoiding the undefined shift behavior for that specific boundary value.

cve_description: XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform offering runtime services for applications built on top of it. Starting with version 8.3-rc-1 and prior to versions 12.10.3 and 14.0, one can ask for any file located in the classloader using the template API and a path with ".." in it. The issue is patched in versions 14.0 and 13.10.3. There is no easy workaround for this issue.
cause_reason: C1 only fixed the path traversal vulnerability in `InternalTemplateManager.getClassloaderTemplate()`, but the same classloader resource access vulnerability existed in other code locations: `WebJarsResourceReferenceHandler.getResourceStream()` and `SxResourceSource.getContent()`. C2 applied the fix (using `ClassLoaderUtils.getResource/getResourceAsStream`) to all three locations, showing C1 missed applying the fix to additional code scopes that had the same vulnerability.

cve_description: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute in GitHub repository ikus060/rdiffweb prior to 2.4.2.
cause_reason: C1 attached the cookie security headers at the 'before_finalize' hook via a HandlerTool, which only runs for successful responses. HTTP error responses (404, redirects like 301/303) bypass this hook, so cookies sent during error/redirect responses lacked the 'Secure' attribute. C2 fixed this by moving the logic to the 'before_request_body' hook, which executes earlier and covers all response paths including errors and redirects.

cve_description: XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform offering runtime services for applications built on top of it. In affected versions there is no protection against URL redirection to untrusted sites, in particular some well known parameters (xredirect) can be used to perform url redirections. This problem has been patched in XWiki 12.10.7 and XWiki 13.3RC1. Users are advised to update. There are no known workarounds for this issue.
cause_reason: C1's domain validation was overly strict, rejecting single-component domains and not automatically trusting the server's own domain, potentially blocking legitimate same-domain redirects.

cve_description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C. A buffer overflow vulnerability in versions 2.12 and prior affects applications that use PJSIP DNS resolution. It doesn't affect PJSIP users who utilize an external resolver. This vulnerability is related to CVE-2023-27585. The difference is that this issue is in parsing the query record `parse_rr()`, while the issue in CVE-2023-27585 is in `parse_query()`. A patch is available in the `master` branch of the `pjsip/pjproject` GitHub repository. A workaround is to disable DNS resolution in PJSIP config (by setting `nameserver_count` to zero) or use an external resolver instead.
cause_reason: C1 fixed bounds checking in get_name_len, get_name, and parse_query functions, but did not apply similar bounds validation to the parse_rr function's record-type-specific branches (A, AAAA, SRV). C2 extends the same bounds-checking pattern to these additional code paths in parse_rr and also adds a start>=max check that C1 had removed from get_name_len/get_name.

cve_description: In Keylime before 6.3.0, Revocation Notifier uses a fixed /tmp path for UNIX domain socket which can allow unprivileged users a method to prohibit keylime operations.
cause_reason: C1 used `_SOCKET_PATH` (the socket file path) instead of `dir_name` (the directory path) in the `os.stat()` call. This is a straightforward wrong variable usage — C2 simply corrects the variable from `_SOCKET_PATH` to `dir_name` to check the directory's permissions instead of the non-existent socket file.

cve_description: Open redirect vulnerability via endpoint authorize_and_redirect/?redirect= in GitHub repository posthog/posthog prior to 1.34.1.
cause_reason: C1 only added the hostname_in_app_urls validation to the authorize_and_redirect endpoint in posthog/urls.py, but did not apply the same redirect validation to the redirect_to_site endpoint in posthog/api/user.py. C2 applies the same hostname_in_allowed_url_list check to the redirect_to_site endpoint, which was a separate code scope with the same open redirect vulnerability.

cve_description: Out-of-bounds Read in Homebrew mruby prior to 3.2.
cause_reason: C1 correctly identified the need to pack arguments into an array when n reaches a boundary value (n==14) but missed the adjacent boundary value n==13, which also has extra arguments (kw and rhs) requiring the same packing logic. C2 extends the condition to include n==13.

cve_description: bluetoothd from bluez incorrectly saves adapters' Discoverable status when a device is powered down, and restores it when powered up. If a device is powered down while discoverable, it will be discoverable when powered on again. This could lead to inadvertent exposure of the bluetooth stack to physically nearby attackers.
cause_reason: C1 used the wrong constant `MGMT_OP_SET_DISCOVERABLE` (an operation code) instead of the correct bitmask constant `MGMT_SETTING_DISCOVERABLE` in two bitwise AND operations against `adapter->current_settings`. This is a wrong constant/name error where the developer picked the wrong identifier from a similar namespace.

cve_description: An issue was discovered in ThoughtWorks GoCD before 21.3.0. An attacker who has compromised a GoCD agent can upload a malicious file into a directory of a GoCD server. They can control the filename but the directory is placed inside of a directory that they can't control.
cause_reason: C1's isValidStageCounter method correctly validated that stageCounter must be a positive integer, but missed the special value 'latest' which is a legitimate semantic input in GoCD's artifact workflow. C2 extends the validation to explicitly allow 'latest' as a valid stageCounter value, which is a specific boundary/special value that C1's validation logic failed to account for.

cve_description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 8.2.
cause_reason: C1 correctly identified the need for multi-byte character alignment but handled the `b_insert` and non-`b_insert` cases separately with different logic. C2 simplified this by recognizing that both cases need the same fix: simply clamp offset using `mb_head_off(oldp, oldp + offset)` regardless of the insert mode. C1's `b_insert` branch adjusted `spaces` and `count` based on `offset + spaces` rather than clamping `offset` itself, which left a path where offset could still exceed the line's end when allocation block sizes are tightly filled.

cve_description: Flatpak is a Linux application sandboxing and distribution framework. A path traversal vulnerability affects versions of Flatpak prior to 1.12.3 and 1.10.6. flatpak-builder applies `finish-args` last in the build. At this point the build directory will have the full access that is specified in the manifest, so running `flatpak build` against it will gain those permissions. Normally this will not be done, so this is not problem. However, if `--mirror-screenshots-url` is specified, then flatpak-builder will launch `flatpak build --nofilesystem=host appstream-utils mirror-screenshots` after finalization, which can lead to issues even with the `--nofilesystem=host` protection. In normal use, the only issue is that these empty directories can be created wherever the user has write permissions. However, a malicious application could replace the `appstream-util` binary and potentially do something more hostile. This has been resolved in Flatpak 1.12.3 and 1.10.6 by changing the behaviour of `--nofilesystem=home` and `--nofilesystem=host`.
cause_reason: C1's fix made --nofilesystem=host/home always remove access recursively, which was too strict and broke backward compatibility. C2 fixed this by requiring an explicit ':all' suffix for recursive removal.

cve_description: If an attacker comes into the possession of a victim's OctoPrint session cookie through whatever means, the attacker can use this cookie to authenticate as long as the victim's account exists.
cause_reason: C1's signature_key_for_user in FilebasedUserManager looked up the username in self._users, but didn't handle the special '_api' username (global API key) which has no corresponding user account. C2 added an explicit check: if username is '_api', fall back to the parent class's simplified key derivation instead of attempting a user lookup that would raise UnknownUser.

cve_description: Use After Free in GitHub repository radareorg/radare2 prior to 5.6.2.
cause_reason: C1's fix was logically flawed — it suppressed the free callback as a workaround rather than fixing the actual logic error. C2 corrects the deletion loop logic by properly tracking submap boundaries (the 'ento' variable) and validating containment before deletion, removing C1's incorrect free-disabling hack. The core issue was incorrect loop logic that accessed freed data, not a wrong variable or API misuse.

cve_description: When ldns version 1.7.1 verifies a zone file, the ldns_rr_new_frm_str_internal function has a heap out of bounds read vulnerability. An attacker can leak information on the heap by constructing a zone file payload.
cause_reason: C1 used the wrong buffer variable (`strbuf`) in bounds checks instead of the correct buffer (`rd_buf`) that was actually being accessed. C2 corrects this by replacing `sldns_buffer_remaining(strbuf)` with `ldns_buffer_remaining(rd_buf)` in both the while loop and if condition.

cve_description: Atheme IRC Services before 7.2.12, when used in conjunction with InspIRCd, allows authentication bypass by ending an IRC handshake at a certain point during a challenge-response login sequence.
cause_reason: C1 correctly introduced pendingeid tracking for the authentication state, but missed the abort/done ('D' command) scenario where sasl_session_destroy would blow away the pendingeid state. C2 fixes this by introducing sasl_session_reset and sasl_session_reset_or_destroy functions that preserve pendingeid during session aborts, ensuring the pending login state survives client abort sequences. This is an exceptional state (session abort) that C1's fix logic didn't account for.

cve_description: png2webp v1.0.4 was discovered to contain an out-of-bounds write via the function w2p. This vulnerability is exploitable via a crafted png file.
cause_reason: C1 used SSIZE_MAX as the upper bound for validation, which on 64-bit systems can be extremely large (2^63-1), failing to properly constrain buffer sizes. C2 fixed this by changing the type to uint32_t and enforcing a concrete upper limit of 0xfffffffe, and also added chunked reading to handle cases where the size exceeds what a single fread can handle (>0x7fffffff). The core issue was that C1's boundary value (SSIZE_MAX) was platform-dependent and insufficient on 64-bit architectures.

cve_description: TensorFlow is an open source platform for machine learning. Prior to versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4, TensorFlow's `saved_model_cli` tool is vulnerable to a code injection. This can be used to open a reverse shell. This code path was maintained for compatibility reasons as the maintainers had several test cases where numpy expressions were used as arguments. However, given that the tool is always run manually, the impact of this is still not severe. The maintainers have now removed the `safe=False` argument, so all parsing is done without calling `eval`. The patch is available in versions 2.9.0, 2.8.1, 2.7.2, and 2.6.4.
cause_reason: C1 introduced a safe=True default parameter for preprocess_input_exprs_arg_string but then explicitly called it with safe=False in the main code path (load_inputs_from_input_arg_string), creating a logical inconsistency where the safety mechanism was defined but deliberately bypassed in the actual execution path.

cve_description: Cross-site Scripting (XSS) - Stored in GitHub repository inventree/inventree prior to 0.8.3.
cause_reason: C1's sanitize_svg function only handled string input but missed the case where file data arrives as bytes. C2 adds a type check and decodes byte-encoded input to string before sanitization, addressing a specific input type edge case that could bypass the sanitization.

cve_description: XWiki Platform Old Core is a core package for XWiki Platform, a generic wiki platform. Prior to versions 14.2 and 13.10.4, all rights checks that would normally prevent a user from viewing a document on a wiki can be bypassed using the login action and directly specified templates. This exposes title, content and comments of any document and properties of objects, though class and property name must be known. This is also exploitable on private wikis. This has been patched in versions 14.2 and 13.10.4 by properly checking view rights before loading documents and disallowing non-default templates in the login, registration and skin action. As a workaround, it would be possible to protect all templates individually by adding code to check access rights first.
cause_reason: C1's validation was too restrictive, blocking all template overrides including legitimate ones like 'registerinline'. C2 refined the check to use an allowlist of safe templates.

cve_description: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in GitHub repository jgraph/drawio prior to 18.0.6.
cause_reason: C1 applied URL sanitization to ProxyServlet and EmbedServlet2 but missed ExportProxyServlet entirely (which was an open proxy to localhost), and also failed to disable redirect following in EmbedServlet2. C2 deleted the vulnerable ExportProxyServlet and added setInstanceFollowRedirects(false) in EmbedServlet2.

cve_description: The package com.alibaba:fastjson before 1.2.83 are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data by bypassing the default autoType shutdown restrictions, which is possible under certain conditions. Exploiting this vulnerability allows attacking remote servers. Workaround: If upgrading is not possible, you can enable [safeMode](https://github.com/alibaba/fastjson/wiki/fastjson_safemode).
cause_reason: C1 blocked Throwable subclasses ending in 'Exception' but missed those ending in 'Error' (e.g., OutOfMemoryError, StackOverflowError). Both Exception and Error are subclasses of Throwable, and C1 only handled the Exception variant. C2 also added conditional gating of TypeUtils.addMapping() calls when autoTypeSupport is disabled, which was another missed condition where cached mappings could bypass security checks.

cve_description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository vim/vim prior to 8.2.
cause_reason: C1 added a NUL check and break inside the loop, but missed a separate code path after the loop where `that++` and `amount++` could still increment past the NUL terminator. C2 guards that specific pointer increment with an additional NUL check, addressing the same vulnerability in a different execution path within the same function that C1's fix didn't cover.

cve_description: It was found that the fix for CVE-2017-7500 and CVE-2017-7501 was incomplete: the check was only implemented for the parent directory of the file to be created. A local unprivileged user who owns another ancestor directory could potentially use this flaw to gain root privileges. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity as well as system availability.
cause_reason: C1 converted only mkdir and directory operations to dirfd-anchored *at() APIs but left symlink, mkfifo, mknod, link, and open still using unsafe path-based syscalls (symlink(), mkfifo(), mknod(), link(), Fopen()). C2 completes the conversion by switching all remaining file creation functions to their *at() variants (symlinkat, mkfifoat, mknodat, linkat, openat), which was the intended security pattern that C1 incompletely applied.

cve_description: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in GitHub repository ikus060/rdiffweb prior to 2.5.0.
cause_reason: C1 applied rate-limiting decorators to login, MFA verification, password change, and API endpoints but missed applying the same rate-limiting decorator to the MFA preferences page (page_pref_mfa.py) that handles the 'Resend code' action. C2 adds the same `@cherrypy.tools.ratelimit(methods=['POST'])` decorator to this previously unprotected endpoint, demonstrating a breadth problem where the same fix pattern wasn't applied to all code scopes that needed it.

cve_description: Use After Free in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to v2.1.0-DEV.
cause_reason: C1 called gf_node_unregister (the wrong function) instead of gf_node_register. The comment even says 'register TWICE' but the code calls unregister twice, which is a direct wrong function/API call that causes the node to be freed rather than retained.

cve_description: Redis is an open source, in-memory database that persists on disk. In affected versions specially crafted Lua scripts executing in Redis can cause the heap-based Lua stack to be overflowed, due to incomplete checks for this condition. This can result with heap corruption and potentially remote code execution. This problem exists in all versions of Redis with Lua scripting support, starting from 2.6. The problem is fixed in versions 6.2.6, 6.0.16 and 5.0.14. For users unable to update an additional workaround to mitigate the problem without patching the redis-server executable is to prevent users from executing Lua scripts. This can be done using ACL to restrict EVAL and EVALSHA commands.
cause_reason: C1 added lua_checkstack checks to only three functions (redisProtocolToLuaType, redisProtocolToLuaType_Aggregate, luaReplyToRedisReply, ldbRedis), but C2 applied the same lua_checkstack pattern to many additional helper functions (redisProtocolToLuaType_Int, _NullBulkString, _NullArray, _BulkString, _Status, _Error, _Map, _Set, _Array, _VerbatimString, _BigNumber, _Null, _Bool, _Double) that also push elements onto the Lua stack and could be exploited to cause stack overflow.

cve_description: Redash is a package for data visualization and sharing. In versions 10.0 and priorm the implementation of URL-loading data sources like JSON, CSV, or Excel is vulnerable to advanced methods of Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF). These vulnerabilities are only exploitable on installations where a URL-loading data source is enabled. As of time of publication, the `master` and `release/10.x.x` branches address this by applying the Advocate library for making http requests instead of the requests library directly. Users should upgrade to version 10.0.1 to receive this patch. There are a few workarounds for mitigating the vulnerability without upgrading. One can disable the vulnerable data sources entirely, by adding the following env variable to one's configuration, making them unavailable inside the webapp. One can switch any data source of certain types (viewable in the GitHub Security Advisory) to be `View Only` for all groups on the Settings > Groups > Data Sources screen. For users unable to update an admin may modify Redash's configuration through environment variables to mitigate this issue. Depending on the version of Redash, an admin may also need to run a CLI command to re-encrypt some fields in the database. The `master` and `release/10.x.x` branches as of time of publication have removed the default value for `REDASH_COOKIE_SECRET`. All future releases will also require this to be set explicitly. For existing installations, one will need to ensure that explicit values are set for the `REDASH_COOKIE_SECRET` and `REDASH_SECRET_KEY `variables.
cause_reason: C1 correctly introduced the advocate library for SSRF protection, but failed to ensure the dependency was properly declared in the project's canonical dependency management file (pyproject.toml/poetry.lock). A subsequent commit removed advocate because it wasn't properly tracked, reintroducing the vulnerability. C2 restores advocate by adding it to both pyproject.toml and poetry.lock, ensuring the security dependency persists.

cve_description: In RELIC before 2021-04-03, there is a buffer overflow in PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification because garbage bytes can be present.
cause_reason: C1 accumulated XOR differences in variable 'r' (where r==0 means valid match) but then checked 'if (r && m_len > 0)' to accept the signature, inverting the acceptance condition. C2 corrects this to 'if (r == 0 && m_len > 0)', fixing the logical inconsistency between what 'r' represents and how it was evaluated.

cve_description: Sydent is a reference Matrix identity server. Sydent can be induced to send HTTP GET requests to internal systems, due to lack of parameter validation or IP address blacklisting. It is not possible to exfiltrate data or control request headers, but it might be possible to use the attack to perform an internal port enumeration. This issue has been addressed in in 9e57334, 8936925, 3d531ed, 0f00412. A potential workaround would be to use a firewall to ensure that Sydent cannot reach internal HTTP resources.
cause_reason: C1's validation was too restrictive, rejecting valid IP addresses and IPv6 literals that are allowed by Matrix spec, while C2 broadened the validation to accept all valid Matrix server names.

cve_description: In Calibre-web, versions 0.6.0 to 0.6.13 are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). By luring an authenticated user to click on a link, an attacker can create a new user role with admin privileges and attacker-controlled credentials, allowing them to take over the application.
cause_reason: C1 correctly implemented the CSRF protection logic and dependency check, but commented out the sys.exit(7) call that enforces the dependency requirement. This is a semantic/configuration error where the enforcement mechanism was intentionally weakened (commented out), allowing the application to run without CSRF protection despite having the check in place.

cve_description: Micronaut is a JVM-based, full stack Java framework designed for building JVM applications. A path traversal vulnerability exists in versions prior to 2.5.9. With a basic configuration, it is possible to access any file from a filesystem, using "/../../" in the URL. This occurs because Micronaut does not restrict file access to configured paths. The vulnerability is patched in version 2.5.9. As a workaround, do not use `**` in mapping, use only `*`, which exposes only flat structure of a directory not allowing traversal. If using Linux, another workaround is to run micronaut in chroot.
cause_reason: C1's classpath protection relied on URL-based containment checks (startsWithBase) which don't work reliably in all JVM implementations (e.g., GraalVM where baseURL may be null). C2 added an alternative protection path: when checkBase is false (the default), it uses isProhibitedRelativePath() to explicitly block '../' patterns in paths, ensuring path traversal is prevented even when URL-based base validation is unavailable or unreliable.

cve_description: In Django 2.2 before 2.2.21, 3.1 before 3.1.9, and 3.2 before 3.2.1, MultiPartParser, UploadedFile, and FieldFile allowed directory traversal via uploaded files with suitably crafted file names.
cause_reason: C1's validation rejected all path separators in filenames, blocking both malicious traversal attempts and legitimate relative paths from upload_to() functions. C2 refined this by allowing relative paths without '..' segments.

cve_description: An issue was discovered in gpac before 1.0.1. The abst_box_read function in box_code_adobe.c has a heap-based buffer over-read.
cause_reason: C1 corrected the buffer size calculation but failed to allocate an extra byte for the null terminator, resulting in a buffer size miscalculation. C2 fixes this by allocating tmp_strsize+1 bytes and explicitly null-terminating the string, addressing the classic off-by-one allocation mismatch for C-string buffers.

cve_description: A flaw was found in RPM's signature check functionality when reading a package file. This flaw allows an attacker who can convince a victim to install a seemingly verifiable package, whose signature header was modified, to cause RPM database corruption and execute code. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data integrity, confidentiality, and system availability.
cause_reason: C1's validation was overly strict in rejecting any presence of certain tags in the main header, failing to account for legitimate legacy packages where these tags naturally resided there.

cve_description: Zope is an open-source web application server. In Zope versions prior to 4.6 and 5.2, users can access untrusted modules indirectly through Python modules that are available for direct use. By default, only users with the Manager role can add or edit Zope Page Templates through the web, but sites that allow untrusted users to add/edit Zope Page Templates through the web are at risk from this vulnerability. The problem has been fixed in Zope 5.2 and 4.6. As a workaround, a site administrator can restrict adding/editing Zope Page Templates through the web using the standard Zope user/role permission mechanisms. Untrusted users should not be assigned the Zope Manager role and adding/editing Zope Page Templates through the web should be restricted to trusted users only.
cause_reason: C1 correctly blocked names starting with underscores, but missed the broader attack vector: traversal through authorized Python modules to unauthorized sub-objects (e.g., `modules/AccessControl/users`) that don't involve underscore-prefixed names. C2 added explicit `validate()` security checks on all traversePathElement results in the non-ITraversable code path, catching the case where traversal to legitimate names still leads to unauthorized access without underscore prefixes.

cve_description: Synapse is a Matrix reference homeserver written in python (pypi package matrix-synapse). Matrix is an ecosystem for open federated Instant Messaging and VoIP. In Synapse before version 1.25.0, requests to user provided domains were not restricted to external IP addresses when calculating the key validity for third-party invite events and sending push notifications. This could cause Synapse to make requests to internal infrastructure. The type of request was not controlled by the user, although limited modification of request bodies was possible. For the most thorough protection server administrators should remove the deprecated `federation_ip_range_blacklist` from their settings after upgrading to Synapse v1.25.0 which will result in Synapse using the improved default IP address restrictions. See the new `ip_range_blacklist` and `ip_range_whitelist` settings if more specific control is necessary.
cause_reason: C1 introduced `ip_range_blacklist` but left it as an opt-in configuration requiring manual setup. The default was an empty list, meaning unconfigured instances had no IP blacklist protection. C2 fixed this by making `ip_range_blacklist` default to `DEFAULT_IP_RANGE_BLACKLIST` (private IP ranges) when not explicitly configured, ensuring security by default without manual intervention.

cve_description: dbeaver is vulnerable to Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
cause_reason: C1 set the secure processing feature on the DocumentBuilderFactory AFTER creating the DocumentBuilder, meaning the builder was created without the security feature applied. C2 corrects the execution order by moving setFeature before newDocumentBuilder(), which is a classic wrong execution order / semantic misunderstanding of how the factory-builder pattern works.

cve_description: app/views_mod/user/user.py in LibrIT PaSSHport through 2.5 is affected by LDAP Injection. There is an information leak through the crafting of special queries, escaping the provided search filter because user input gets no sanitization.
cause_reason: C1 used escape_rdn() which is designed for escaping LDAP Distinguished Name components, not LDAP filter expressions. C2 corrects this by replacing it with escape_filter_chars(), which is the appropriate API for escaping special characters in LDAP filter contexts.

cve_description: Netty is an open-source, asynchronous event-driven network application framework for rapid development of maintainable high performance protocol servers & clients. In Netty (io.netty:netty-codec-http2) before version 4.1.60.Final there is a vulnerability that enables request smuggling. If a Content-Length header is present in the original HTTP/2 request, the field is not validated by `Http2MultiplexHandler` as it is propagated up. This is fine as long as the request is not proxied through as HTTP/1.1. If the request comes in as an HTTP/2 stream, gets converted into the HTTP/1.1 domain objects (`HttpRequest`, `HttpContent`, etc.) via `Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec `and then sent up to the child channel's pipeline and proxied through a remote peer as HTTP/1.1 this may result in request smuggling. In a proxy case, users may assume the content-length is validated somehow, which is not the case. If the request is forwarded to a backend channel that is a HTTP/1.1 connection, the Content-Length now has meaning and needs to be checked. An attacker can smuggle requests inside the body as it gets downgraded from HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1. For an example attack refer to the linked GitHub Advisory. Users are only affected if all of this is true: `HTTP2MultiplexCodec` or `Http2FrameCodec` is used, `Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec` is used to convert to HTTP/1.1 objects, and these HTTP/1.1 objects are forwarded to another remote peer. This has been patched in 4.1.60.Final As a workaround, the user can do the validation by themselves by implementing a custom `ChannelInboundHandler` that is put in the `ChannelPipeline` behind `Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec`.
cause_reason: C1 unconditionally called headers.set(CONTENT_LENGTH, contentLength) even when the original single Content-Length value was already valid and correct. C2 fixes this by adding a conditional check to only rewrite the header when there are multiple Content-Length fields or the value actually differs, preventing unnecessary header reordering. This is a logic flaw where C1 failed to distinguish between cases needing normalization and cases that were already correct.

cve_description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In affected versions if the incoming STUN message contains an ERROR-CODE attribute, the header length is not checked before performing a subtraction operation, potentially resulting in an integer underflow scenario. This issue affects all users that use STUN. A malicious actor located within the victim’s network may forge and send a specially crafted UDP (STUN) message that could remotely execute arbitrary code on the victim’s machine. Users are advised to upgrade as soon as possible. There are no known workarounds.
cause_reason: C1 checked if value.slen < 0 after subtraction (allowing underflow to occur), while C2 correctly checks if attr->hdr.length < 4 before subtraction (preventing underflow).

cve_description: An issue was discovered in GPAC before 0.8.0, as demonstrated by MP4Box. It contains an invalid memory read in gf_m2ts_process_pmt in media_tools/mpegts.c that can cause a denial of service via a crafted MP4 file.
cause_reason: C1 only restructured conditional logic (moved stream type counting inside a brace block) but completely missed adding bounds checks on input data sizes. C2 added explicit size validation checks (e.g., `data_size < 6`, `sec->length < 2`, `desc_len > data_size-5`, loop bound `pos<data_size-5`) to prevent invalid memory reads when processing malformed/truncated PMT data. These are boundary value checks on data length that C1 failed to include.

cve_description: Flatpak is a system for building, distributing, and running sandboxed desktop applications on Linux. In Flatpack since version 0.9.4 and before version 1.10.2 has a vulnerability in the "file forwarding" feature which can be used by an attacker to gain access to files that would not ordinarily be allowed by the app's permissions. By putting the special tokens `@@` and/or `@@u` in the Exec field of a Flatpak app's .desktop file, a malicious app publisher can trick flatpak into behaving as though the user had chosen to open a target file with their Flatpak app, which automatically makes that file available to the Flatpak app. This is fixed in version 1.10.2. A minimal solution is the first commit "`Disallow @@ and @@U usage in desktop files`". The follow-up commits "`dir: Reserve the whole @@ prefix`" and "`dir: Refuse to export .desktop files with suspicious uses of @@ tokens`" are recommended, but not strictly required. As a workaround, avoid installing Flatpak apps from untrusted sources, or check the contents of the exported `.desktop` files in `exports/share/applications/*.desktop` (typically `~/.local/share/flatpak/exports/share/applications/*.desktop` and `/var/lib/flatpak/exports/share/applications/*.desktop`) to make sure that literal filenames do not follow `@@` or `@@u`.
cause_reason: C1 only blocked the exact tokens '@@' and '@@u' via exact string matching, but missed other possible @@-prefixed variants (e.g., '@@x', '@@foo') that could be used as attack vectors. C2 replaced the exact matches with a prefix check (g_str_has_prefix(arg, "@@")) to cover all @@-prefixed arguments.

cve_description: PJSIP is a free and open source multimedia communication library written in C language implementing standard based protocols such as SIP, SDP, RTP, STUN, TURN, and ICE. In version 2.10 and earlier, PJSIP transport can be reused if they have the same IP address + port + protocol. However, this is insufficient for secure transport since it lacks remote hostname authentication. Suppose we have created a TLS connection to `sip.foo.com`, which has an IP address `100.1.1.1`. If we want to create a TLS connection to another hostname, say `sip.bar.com`, which has the same IP address, then it will reuse that existing connection, even though `100.1.1.1` does not have certificate to authenticate as `sip.bar.com`. The vulnerability allows for an insecure interaction without user awareness. It affects users who need access to connections to different destinations that translate to the same address, and allows man-in-the-middle attack if attacker can route a connection to another destination such as in the case of DNS spoofing.
cause_reason: C1 captured initial_dest from all transports without distinguishing direction, missing the edge case where incoming connections would overwrite the destination hostname. C2 adds a check for `PJSIP_TP_DIR_OUTGOING` to ensure only outgoing transport directions are used for capturing the initial destination host, preventing incoming connections from corrupting the hostname used for TLS certificate verification.

cve_description: The flash read-out protection (RDP) level is not enforced during the device initialization phase of the SoloKeys Solo 4.0.0 & Somu and the Nitrokey FIDO2 token. This allows an adversary to downgrade the RDP level and access secrets such as private ECC keys from SRAM via the debug interface.
cause_reason: C1 had two distinct issues: (1) wrong execution order — calling flash_option_bytes_init() before device_migrate() — and (2) failing to unlock the flash option bytes controller before writing to FLASH->CR, plus using an exact comparison instead of a masked comparison. This combination of initialization ordering and missing hardware unlock sequence is best described as 'improper hardware register access sequencing' — the flash option byte controller was not unlocked before the write, causing a hang, which doesn't fit the existing L2 sub-patterns well. It's a hardware peripheral initialization protocol violation.

cve_description: In “Calibre-web” application, v0.6.0 to v0.6.12, are vulnerable to Stored XSS in “Metadata”. An attacker that has access to edit the metadata information, can inject JavaScript payload in the description field. When a victim tries to open the file, XSS will be triggered.
cause_reason: C1 used lxml.html.clean.clean_html without any error handling. C2 adds try-except blocks to catch TypeError (when lxml is too new/incompatible) and ParserError (corrupted comments), with fallback sanitization libraries (bleach/nh3). C1 missed the exceptional states where the sanitization call itself could fail, causing the XSS fix to be bypassed.

cve_description: Scrapy is a high-level web crawling and scraping framework for Python. If you use `HttpAuthMiddleware` (i.e. the `http_user` and `http_pass` spider attributes) for HTTP authentication, all requests will expose your credentials to the request target. This includes requests generated by Scrapy components, such as `robots.txt` requests sent by Scrapy when the `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY` setting is set to `True`, or as requests reached through redirects. Upgrade to Scrapy 2.5.1 and use the new `http_auth_domain` spider attribute to control which domains are allowed to receive the configured HTTP authentication credentials. If you are using Scrapy 1.8 or a lower version, and upgrading to Scrapy 2.5.1 is not an option, you may upgrade to Scrapy 1.8.1 instead. If you cannot upgrade, set your HTTP authentication credentials on a per-request basis, using for example the `w3lib.http.basic_auth_header` function to convert your credentials into a value that you can assign to the `Authorization` header of your request, instead of defining your credentials globally using `HttpAuthMiddleware`.
cause_reason: C1's validation was too permissive - it allowed `http_auth_domain` to be optional with a fallback mechanism, enabling continued insecure operation. C2 made it mandatory, properly restricting credentials to specified domains only.

cve_description: NULL Pointer Deference in the exif command line tool, when printing out XML formatted EXIF data, in exif v0.6.22 and earlier allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by uploading a malicious JPEG file, causing the application to crash.
cause_reason: C1's validation check was too permissive - it called strlen() without first checking if text was NULL, allowing NULL pointers to cause crashes. C2 fixed the condition logic to check for NULL first.

cve_description: Fluent Bit (aka fluent-bit) 1.7.0 through 1.7.4 has a double free in flb_free (called from flb_parser_json_do and flb_parser_do).
cause_reason: C1 added `flb_free(tmp_out_buf)` alongside `flb_free(mp_buf)` in the error handling block but missed the edge case where mp_buf and tmp_out_buf are aliased (point to the same memory). C2 adds a conditional check `if (mp_buf == tmp_out_buf)` to only free once when the pointers are identical, preventing the double-free.

cve_description: Flask-AppBuilder is an application development framework, built on top of Flask. In affected versions if using Flask-AppBuilder OAuth, an attacker can share a carefully crafted URL with a trusted domain for an application built with Flask-AppBuilder, this URL can redirect a user to a malicious site. This is an open redirect vulnerability. To resolve this issue upgrade to Flask-AppBuilder 3.2.2 or above. If upgrading is infeasible users may filter HTTP traffic containing `?next={next-site}` where the `next-site` domain is different from the application you are protecting as a workaround.
cause_reason: C1 correctly fixed the open redirect vulnerability in the OAuth authentication flow (oauth_authorized), but failed to apply the same URL validation to the other authentication methods: AuthDBView, AuthLDAPView, and AuthOIDView. C2 introduced a centralized get_safe_redirect utility and applied it across all four authentication paths.

cve_description: Netty is an open-source, asynchronous event-driven network application framework for rapid development of maintainable high performance protocol servers & clients. In Netty before version 4.1.59.Final there is a vulnerability on Unix-like systems involving an insecure temp file. When netty's multipart decoders are used local information disclosure can occur via the local system temporary directory if temporary storing uploads on the disk is enabled. On unix-like systems, the temporary directory is shared between all user. As such, writing to this directory using APIs that do not explicitly set the file/directory permissions can lead to information disclosure. Of note, this does not impact modern MacOS Operating Systems. The method "File.createTempFile" on unix-like systems creates a random file, but, by default will create this file with the permissions "-rw-r--r--". Thus, if sensitive information is written to this file, other local users can read this information. This is the case in netty's "AbstractDiskHttpData" is vulnerable. This has been fixed in version 4.1.59.Final. As a workaround, one may specify your own "java.io.tmpdir" when you start the JVM or use "DefaultHttpDataFactory.setBaseDir(...)" to set the directory to something that is only readable by the current user.
cause_reason: C1's Java 6 fallback path only applied permission restrictions when a directory was specified (non-null), but missed the case when directory was null. C2 fixes this by applying setReadable() to both the null and non-null directory paths on Java 6, and also adds proper error handling by throwing IOException if setReadable() fails.

cve_description: An issue was discovered in SKALE sgxwallet 1.58.3. sgx_disp_ippsAES_GCMEncrypt allows an out-of-bounds write, resulting in a segfault and compromised enclave. This issue describes a buffer overflow, which was resolved prior to v1.77.0 and not reproducible in latest sgxwallet v1.77.0
cause_reason: C1 changed variable types from uint32_t to uint64_t and restructured AES_encrypt to include type/decryptable fields and resultLen parameter, but failed to add critical runtime validation logic: NULL check for resultLen parameter, enc_len validation against actual buffer length in trustedDecryptKey, and proper bounds checking. C2 completes the fix by adding these missing validation checks and correcting the logic flow.

cve_description: Varnish Cache, with HTTP/2 enabled, allows request smuggling and VCL authorization bypass via a large Content-Length header for a POST request. This affects Varnish Enterprise 6.0.x before 6.0.8r3, and Varnish Cache 5.x and 6.x before 6.5.2, 6.6.x before 6.6.1, and 6.0 LTS before 6.0.8.
cause_reason: C1's fix was architecturally fragile - it implemented Content-Length validation using a simple byte counter tied to the synchronous mailcall mechanism. C2 had to completely re-implement the same validation logic within a new asynchronous ring buffer architecture (h2_rxbuf) because C1's approach was semantically incompatible with proper HTTP/2 data flow handling, including incorrect handling of zero-length frames, state transitions, and window management.

cve_description: Zope is an open-source web application server. This advisory extends the previous advisory at https://github.com/zopefoundation/Zope/security/advisories/GHSA-5pr9-v234-jw36 with additional cases of TAL expression traversal vulnerabilities. Most Python modules are not available for using in TAL expressions that you can add through-the-web, for example in Zope Page Templates. This restriction avoids file system access, for example via the 'os' module. But some of the untrusted modules are available indirectly through Python modules that are available for direct use. By default, you need to have the Manager role to add or edit Zope Page Templates through the web. Only sites that allow untrusted users to add/edit Zope Page Templates through the web are at risk. The problem has been fixed in Zope 5.2.1 and 4.6.1. The workaround is the same as for https://github.com/zopefoundation/Zope/security/advisories/GHSA-5pr9-v234-jw36: A site administrator can restrict adding/editing Zope Page Templates through the web using the standard Zope user/role permission mechanisms. Untrusted users should not be assigned the Zope Manager role and adding/editing Zope Page Templates through the web should be restricted to trusted users only.
cause_reason: C1 applied the fix (replacing guarded_import with getSecurityManager().validate) only to the Zope 5.x branch. C2 applies the exact same fix pattern to the Zope 4.x branch, which still used the old guarded_import approach with the isinstance(object, ModuleType) check. The vulnerability existed in both version branches but C1 only patched one.

cve_description: ImageMagick is free software delivered as a ready-to-run binary distribution or as source code that you may use, copy, modify, and distribute in both open and proprietary applications. In affected versions and in certain cases, Postscript files could be read and written when specifically excluded by a `module` policy in `policy.xml`. ex. <policy domain="module" rights="none" pattern="PS" />. The issue has been resolved in ImageMagick 7.1.0-7 and in 6.9.12-22. Fortunately, in the wild, few users utilize the `module` policy and instead use the `coder` policy that is also our workaround recommendation: <policy domain="coder" rights="none" pattern="{PS,EPI,EPS,EPSF,EPSI}" />.
cause_reason: C1 used AllPolicyRights which is too permissive and could bypass module restrictions, while C2 correctly narrowed it to ReadPolicyRights|WritePolicyRights to properly enforce the policy.

cve_description: Common is a package of common modules that can be accessed by NIMBLE services. Common before commit number 3b96cb0293d3443b870351945f41d7d55cb34b53 did not properly verify the signature of JSON Web Tokens. This allows someone to forge a valid JWT. Being able to forge JWTs may lead to authentication bypasses. Commit number 3b96cb0293d3443b870351945f41d7d55cb34b53 contains a patch for the issue. As a workaround, one may use the parseClaimsJws method to correctly verify the signature of a JWT.
cause_reason: C1 correctly replaced parse() with parseJws() to enforce signature verification, but parseJws() is a generic method that doesn't strictly enforce that the JWT body contains Claims (as opposed to a plaintext payload). parseClaimsJws() specifically validates that the token is a signed JWT with a Claims body, preventing edge cases where an attacker could craft a JWT with a non-Claims payload type that parseJws() would accept but shouldn't be treated as valid authentication.

cve_description: flb_gzip_compress in flb_gzip.c in Fluent Bit before 1.6.4 has an out-of-bounds write because it does not use the correct calculation of the maximum gzip data-size expansion.
cause_reason: C1's manual heuristic for buffer size calculation (5 bytes per 32KB + headers) could underestimate the required allocation, leading to an out-of-bounds write. C2 fixes this by replacing the fragile manual formula with the library-provided compressBound() function, which guarantees a correct upper bound for the compressed output buffer size.

cve_description: XWiki Platform is a generic wiki platform. Starting in version 11.8-rc-1 and prior to versions 14.4.8, 14.10.6, and 15.2, `Mail.MailConfig` can be edited by any logged-in user by default. Consequently, they can change the mail obfuscation configuration and view and edit the mail sending configuration, including the smtp domain name and credentials. The problem has been patched in XWiki 14.4.8, 14.10.6, and 15.1. As a workaround, the rights of the `Mail.MailConfig` page can be manually updated so that only a set of trusted users can view, edit and delete it (e.g., the `XWiki.XWikiAdminGroup` group).
cause_reason: C1's restrictToAdmin() only handled the case where no rights objects existed (empty list). C2 added fixBadlyInitializedRights() to detect and repair the edge case where a rights object exists but has empty/malformed GROUPS_FIELD_NAME and LEVELS_FIELD_NAME values — a state caused by a bug in the initial C1 fix (XWIKI-20519) that created objects without properly setting their fields during upgrades from specific versions.

cve_description: Keycloak, an open-source identity and access management solution, has a cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the SAML or OIDC providers. The vulnerability can allow an attacker to execute malicious scripts by setting the AssertionConsumerServiceURL value or the redirect_uri.
cause_reason: C1 added scheme validation but compared the scheme directly without lowercasing it first (`!valid.startsWith(scheme + ":")`). C2 fixes this by lowercasing the scheme before comparison (`!valid.startsWith(scheme.toLowerCase() + ":")`), and also ensures the valid redirect URIs themselves are lowercased consistently via `lowerCaseHostname` applied during resolution. This is a classic case-sensitivity edge case where mixed-case scheme names like 'JAVASCRIPT' or 'Custom' could bypass the validation.

cve_description:
ScanCode.io is a server to script and automate software composition analysis with ScanPipe pipelines. Prior to version 32.5.1, the software has a possible command injection vulnerability in the docker fetch process as it allows to append malicious commands in the `docker_reference` parameter.

In the function `scanpipe/pipes/fetch.py:fetch_docker_image` the parameter `docker_reference` is user controllable. The `docker_reference` variable is then passed to the vulnerable function `get_docker_image_platform`.  However, the `get_docker_image_plaform` function constructs a shell command with the passed `docker_reference`. The `pipes.run_command` then executes the shell command without any prior sanitization, making the function vulnerable to command injections. A malicious user who is able to create or add inputs to a project can inject commands. Although the command injections are blind and the user will not receive direct feedback without logs, it is still possible to cause damage to the server/container. The vulnerability appears for example if a malicious user adds a semicolon after the input of `docker://;`, it would allow appending malicious commands.

Version 32.5.1 contains a patch for this issue. The `docker_reference` input should be sanitized to avoid command injections and, as a workaround, one may avoid creating commands with user controlled input directly.
cause_reason: C1's shell=False was overly restrictive, breaking legitimate skopeo commands that require shell features; C2 reverted this while keeping the regex validation that actually prevents the injection.

cve_description: exfatprogs before 1.2.2 allows out-of-bounds memory access, such as in read_file_dentry_set.
cause_reason: C1 applied a static MAX_NAME_DENTRIES=17 cap but didn't account for vendor-specific dentry types (EXFAT_VENDOR_EXT, EXFAT_VENDOR_ALLOC) that can appear in the entry set, nor did it dynamically compute the expected name dentry count from Stream.NameLength. C2 fixes these edge cases by computing name_de_count from the stream's NameLength, explicitly handling vendor entries, and repairing mismatched SecondaryCount values.

cve_description: In ssh in OpenSSH before 9.6, OS command injection might occur if a user name or host name has shell metacharacters, and this name is referenced by an expansion token in certain situations. For example, an untrusted Git repository can have a submodule with shell metacharacters in a user name or host name.
cause_reason: C1 implemented the correct fix pattern (blocklisting shell metacharacters in valid_hostname), but missed including the comma character in the prohibited set. C2 adds the comma to the same strchr() call, completing the blocklist for a specific character value that was overlooked.

cve_description: Bazarr manages and downloads subtitles. In version 1.2.4, the proxy method in bazarr/bazarr/app/ui.py does not validate the user-controlled protocol and url variables and passes them to requests.get() without any sanitization, which leads to a blind server-side request forgery (SSRF). This issue allows for crafting GET requests to internal and external resources on behalf of the server. 1.3.1 contains a partial fix, which limits the vulnerability to HTTP/HTTPS protocols.
cause_reason: C1 used `protocol.lower` (a method reference) instead of `protocol.lower()` (a method call), which is a syntax mistake — missing parentheses. This caused the validation check to always evaluate to True (method object not in list), effectively bypassing the protocol whitelist.

cve_description: mindsdb is a Machine Learning platform to help developers build AI solutions. In affected versions an unsafe extraction is being performed using `tarfile.extractall()` from a remotely retrieved tarball. Which may lead to the writing of the extracted files to an unintended location. Sometimes, the vulnerability is called a TarSlip or a ZipSlip variant. An attacker may leverage this vulnerability to overwrite any local file which the server process has access to. There is no risk of file exposure with this vulnerability. This issue has been addressed in release `23.2.1.0 `. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.
cause_reason: C1 placed the safe_extract() function only in the HTTP utils module and applied it to a single .tar.gz code path, but failed to apply it to other tar extraction points (e.g., byom_handler). C2 moved safe_extract() to a shared utilities module (mindsdb/utilities/fs.py) and applied it across all tar extraction locations, indicating C1's architectural misuse of where to place and invoke the security function.

cve_description: Vim is an open source command line text editor. When getting the count for a normal mode z command, it may overflow for large counts given. Impact is low, user interaction is required and a crash may not even happen in all situations. This issue has been addressed in commit `58f9befca1` which has been included in release version 9.0.2109. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.
cause_reason:
Looking at this case:

**C1's fix**: Added `if (n > LONG_MAX / 10)` check before `n = n * 10 + (nchar - '0')` in `nv_z_get_count()`. This check only prevents overflow from the multiplication (`n * 10`), but doesn't account for when `n == LONG_MAX / 10` and the added digit `(nchar - '0')` causes overflow in the addition step.

**C2's fix**: 
1. Replaced C1's incomplete check in `nv_z_get_count()` with `vim_append_digit_long()` which uses the correct formula `x > ((LONG_MAX - digit) / 10)` — this handles both the multiplication and addition overflow in one check.
2. Also fixed the **same type of bug** in `get_number()` in `misc1.c`, replacing `if (n > INT_MAX / 10)` with `vim_append_digit_int()` which uses `x > ((INT_MAX - digit) / 10)`.

C2 does two things: (a) fixes the boundary condition logic in `normal.c` (edge case), and (b) applies the same fix to `misc1.c::get_number()` (breadth). However, the CVE specifically concerns the z command overflow in `normal.c`. The fix to `get_number()` in `misc1.c` is an additional location with the same flawed pattern.

The primary issue is that C1's overflow check formula was mathematically incomplete — it missed the boundary condition where `n == LONG_MAX / 10` and adding a large digit overflows. This is a missing boundary value problem: the check didn't properly handle the exact boundary where `n * 10` succeeds but `n * 10 + digit` overflows.

{"l1": "edge_case_missed", "l2": "missing_boundary_values", "reason": "C1's check `n > LONG_MAX / 10` only prevented overflow from multiplication, but missed the boundary case where n == LONG_MAX/10 and the subsequent addition of the digit causes overflow

cve_description: Vyper is a pythonic Smart Contract Language for the ethereum virtual machine. In contracts with more than one regular nonpayable function, it is possible to send funds to the default function, even if the default function is marked `nonpayable`. This applies to contracts compiled with vyper versions prior to 0.3.8. This issue was fixed by the removal of the global `calldatasize` check in commit `02339dfda`. Users are advised to upgrade to version 0.3.8. Users unable to upgrade should avoid use of nonpayable default functions.
cause_reason: C1 only checked for the exact case where the method selector value was 0, but missed selectors with trailing zero bytes (e.g., 0xd88e0b00). These selectors can also be falsely matched when calldatasize < 4 because calldataload pads with zeros. C2 broadened the check to any selector ending with zero bytes, not just selector == 0.

cve_description: A vulnerability classified as critical has been found in JATOS. Affected is the function ZipUtil of the file modules/common/app/utils/common/ZipUtil.java of the component ZIP Handler. The manipulation leads to path traversal. Upgrading to version 3.7.5-alpha is able to address this issue. The name of the patch is 2b42519f309d8164e8811392770ce604cdabb5da. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The identifier of this vulnerability is VDB-217548.
cause_reason: C1 correctly identified path traversal as the threat and normalized the destination directory, but missed that the attack vector comes from malicious filenames within ZIP entries (e.g., '../../etc/passwd'). C2 adds per-entry canonical path validation to ensure no extracted file escapes the destination directory, addressing the specific attack variant that C1's destDir normalization alone could not prevent.

cve_description: XWiki Rendering is a generic Rendering system that converts textual input in a given syntax into another syntax.
