In the worst case, this could allow a malicious to add malicious script macros including Groovy or Python macros to a page that are then executed after another user with programming righs edits the page, thus allowing remote code execution. The required rights analyzers have been made more robust and extended to cover those cases in XWiki 16.4.7, 16.10.3 and 17.0.0.
cause_reason: C1 only analyzed parameters whose type was exactly Block.LIST_BLOCK_TYPE, hardcoding the check for that single type. C2 introduced an extensible component-based system (MacroParameterRequiredRightsAnalyzer) that handles additional parameter types like MacroContentSourceReference (for script source parameters in content/context macros). C1's fix was correct for wiki syntax parameters but missed other parameter types that could contain dangerous content, which is a depth problem of not considering variant parameter types within the same analysis logic.

cve_description: RomM is a self-hosted rom manager and player. Versions prior to 3.10.3 and 4.0.0-beta.3 have an authenticated path traversal vulnerability in the `/api/raw` endpoint. Anyone running the latest version of RomM and has multiple users, even unprivileged users, such as the kiosk user in the official implementation, may be affected. This allows the leakage of passwords and users that may be stored on the system. Versions 3.10.3 and 4.0.0-beta.3 contain a patch.
cause_reason: C1 correctly implemented validate_and_resolve_path with all necessary checks (absolute path, parent directory references, is_relative_to), but C2 shows that an intermediate version of the code existed that only used `str(requested_path).startswith(str(base_path))` without the absolute path check or parent directory reference check. C2 adds back the missing checks and replaces the weaker `startswith` string comparison with the proper `is_relative_to` method, indicating C1's deployed version had incomplete validation logic that could be bypassed.

cve_description: wiretap/cosine.c in the CoSine file parser in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.12 and 2.x before 2.0.4 mishandles sscanf unsigned-integer processing, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted file.
cause_reason: C1 changed pkt_len to unsigned (guint) with %9u format specifier, but sscanf's %u still accepts negative input strings like '-1' and converts them to large unsigned values. C2 reverts to signed int with %9d and adds an explicit check for pkt_len < 0, properly handling the negative value edge case that C1's approach missed.

cve_description: The read_boot function in boot.c in dosfstools before 4.0 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (crash) via a crafted filesystem, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow in the (1) read_fat function or an out-of-bounds heap read in (2) get_fat function.
cause_reason: C1 correctly changed fat_length and fat_size to off_t and added a zero check, but missed validating that intermediate arithmetic expressions (fat_length * logical_sector_size, reserved + fats * fat_length, etc.) could overflow the off_t type. C2 added explicit OFF_MAX overflow checks on all these arithmetic results before assignment, addressing the missing integer overflow boundary validation that C1 omitted.

cve_description: Integer overflow in Git before 2.7.4 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via a (1) long filename or (2) many nested trees, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.
cause_reason: C1 simplified the callback interface to pass pre-built full pathnames, but did not modify the vulnerable path_name() function itself, which still contained integer overflow-prone manual buffer size calculations (len += p->elem_len + 1 in a loop). C2 completed the fix by replacing path_name()'s vulnerable manual arithmetic with strbuf-based safe buffer management, eliminating the integer overflow that could occur with deeply nested trees or long filenames.

cve_description: Integer overflow in the ImagingResampleHorizontal function in libImaging/Resample.c in Pillow before 3.1.1 allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via negative values of the new size, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.
cause_reason: C1 placed the xbounds overflow check after malloc(kk), creating a memory leak on the error path, and used 'xsize * kmax' in a condition that could itself overflow. These are logical ordering and validation logic errors — the checks were conceptually right but incorrectly structured and sequenced, which C2 fixes by reordering checks before allocations and rewriting the condition to avoid intermediate overflow.

cve_description: epan/crypt/airpdcap.c in the IEEE 802.11 dissector in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.12 and 2.x before 2.0.4 mishandles the lack of an EAPOL_RSN_KEY, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted packet.
cause_reason: C1 used `sizeof(EAPOL_RSN_KEY)` which is the wrong constant/expression for the bounds check, as the struct size varies across versions. C2 corrects it to `RSN_KEY_WITHOUT_KEYBYTES_LEN`, the proper version-agnostic constant that accurately represents the minimum required body length.

cve_description: wiretap/toshiba.c in the Toshiba file parser in Wireshark 1.12.x before 1.12.12 and 2.x before 2.0.4 mishandles sscanf unsigned-integer processing, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted file.
cause_reason: C1 used sscanf with %u format specifier and guint type, misunderstanding that sscanf's %u parsing accepts negative input strings and wraps them to large unsigned values. C2 corrects this by reverting to %d with signed int and adding an explicit negative check, properly handling sscanf's actual behavior.

cve_description: The read_image_tga function in gd_tga.c in the GD Graphics Library (aka libgd) before 2.2.3 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read) via a crafted TGA image.
cause_reason: C1 added bounds checks only against image_block_size (the output bitmap buffer) but missed validating reads against rle_size (the input decompression buffer size). C2 added the complementary buffer_caret + size > rle_size checks to the same bounds-checking conditions in both RLE and non-RLE branches, catching the case where the decompression buffer could be read out-of-bounds even when bitmap checks passed.

cve_description: The (1) EC2 and (2) OS APIs in OpenStack Compute (Nova) Folsom (2012.2), Essex (2012.1), and Diablo (2011.3) do not properly check the protocol when security groups are created and the network protocol is not specified entirely in lowercase, which allows remote attackers to bypass intended access restrictions.
cause_reason: C1 correctly applied .lower() to normalize the protocol field but missed the case where rule.protocol is None (for source-group-based rules without a specified protocol). C2 adds a None check before calling .lower(), handling this null/missing value edge case.

cve_description: do_tgs_req.c in the Key Distribution Center (KDC) in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) 1.11 before 1.11.4, when a single-component realm name is used, allows remote authenticated users to cause a denial of service (daemon crash) via a TGS-REQ request that triggers an attempted cross-realm referral for a host-based service principal.
cause_reason: C1 checked 'server_ptr == NULL' (the pointer itself) instead of '*server_ptr == NULL' (the dereferenced value). C2 corrects this by adding the dereference operator '*' to properly check the value pointed to by server_ptr.

cve_description: The main function in tools/hv/hv_kvp_daemon.c in hypervkvpd, as distributed in the Linux kernel before 3.8-rc1, allows local users to cause a denial of service (daemon exit) via a crafted application that sends a Netlink message.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2012-2669.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed the vulnerability in hv_kvp_daemon.c but the same vulnerability existed in hv_vss_daemon.c. The follow-up patch applied the identical fix to the different daemon file that was missed in the original patch.

cve_description: Use-after-free vulnerability in drivers/net/ppp/ppp_generic.c in the Linux kernel before 4.5.2 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption and system crash, or spinlock) or possibly have unspecified other impact by removing a network namespace, related to the ppp_register_net_channel and ppp_unregister_channel functions.
cause_reason: The original patch incorrectly placed the put_net() call in the unregister function where the channel might still be in use, but the follow-up fix moves it to the destroy function where the channel is actually being freed, showing the original logic was flawed regarding the proper lifecycle management.

cve_description: Buffer Overflow vulnerability in Ffmpeg before github commit 4565747056a11356210ed8edcecb920105e40b60 allows a remote attacker to achieve an out-of-array write, execute arbitrary code, and cause a denial of service (DoS) via the ref_pic_list_struct function in libavcodec/evc_ps.c
cause_reason: The original patch used RAII_VAR with ast_free for real_path but missed that realpath() returns memory allocated by malloc/calloc, requiring ast_std_free instead. This is an exceptional state where the memory allocator differs from the expected cleanup function at the same code location.

cve_description: Asterisk is an open source private branch exchange and telephony toolkit. In Asterisk prior to versions 18.20.1, 20.5.1, and 21.0.1, as well as certified-asterisk prior to 18.9-cert6, it is possible to read any arbitrary file even when the `live_dangerously` is not enabled. This allows arbitrary files to be read. Asterisk versions 18.20.1, 20.5.1, and 21.0.1, as well as certified-asterisk prior to 18.9-cert6, contain a fix for this issue.
cause_reason: The patch incorrectly uses ast_free to deallocate memory returned by realpath(), when it should use ast_std_free since realpath() allocates memory using standard malloc().

cve_description: The LDP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.3 has a buffer over-read in print-ldp.c:ldp_tlv_print().
cause_reason: The original fix changed TLV_TCHECK from 8 to 12 bytes but kept the same error handling mechanism that only printed a generic truncation message. The follow-up fix adds specific boundary value validation that prints the actual TLV length versus required minimum when the boundary condition fails.

cve_description: The bridge multicast implementation in the Linux kernel through 3.10.3 does not check whether a certain timer is armed before modifying the timeout value of that timer, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (BUG and system crash) via vectors involving the shutdown of a KVM virtual machine, related to net/bridge/br_mdb.c and net/bridge/br_multicast.c.
cause_reason: The initial patch added mp->timer_armed checks to two functions but missed the same timer handling issue in other functions like br_multicast_leave_group. The follow-up patch removed the timer_armed field entirely and fixed the broader timer management logic across multiple functions.

cve_description: The bad_mode function in arch/arm64/kernel/traps.c in the Linux kernel before 3.9.5 on the ARM64 platform allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) via vectors involving an attempted register access that triggers an unexpected value in the Exception Syndrome Register (ESR).
cause_reason: C1 changed bad_mode() for all exceptions but only considered EL0 case. C2 splits into bad_mode() (kernel) and bad_el0_sync() (userspace).

cve_description: The Crypto API in the Linux kernel before 3.18.5 allows local users to load arbitrary kernel modules via a bind system call for an AF_ALG socket with a module name in the salg_name field, a different vulnerability than CVE-2014-9644.
cause_reason: The initial patch (C1) changed MODULE_ALIAS to MODULE_ALIAS_CRYPTO across many crypto modules but missed some modules entirely. The follow-up patch (C2) shows the same fix being applied to additional modules and adding missing aliases that were completely omitted in the first pass.

cve_description: During a renegotiation handshake if the Encrypt-Then-Mac extension is negotiated where it was not in the original handshake (or vice-versa) then this can cause OpenSSL 1.1.0 before 1.1.0e to crash (dependent on ciphersuite). Both clients and servers are affected.
cause_reason: The CVE patch introduced separate read/write ETM flags but the follow-up diff adds an assertion mechanism (ossl_assert), indicating the original fix may have missed assertion-related code paths or validation scenarios that needed similar ETM handling.

cve_description: The command-line argument parser in tcpdump before 4.9.3 has a buffer overflow in tcpdump.c:get_next_file().
cause_reason: The original code checked for newline character without first verifying that the string has non-zero length, potentially causing out-of-bounds access when strlen(ptr) is 0. The fix adds a length check before accessing ptr[len-1], placing the boundary check in the correct order.

cve_description: Copyparty is a portable file server. Versions prior to 1.8.2 are subject to a path traversal vulnerability detected in the `.cpr` subfolder. The Path Traversal attack technique allows an attacker access to files, directories, and commands that reside outside the web document root directory. This issue has been addressed in commit `043e3c7d` which has been included in release 1.8.2. Users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.
cause_reason: The original patch checked for path traversal after resolving the path, but the follow-up shows this check needed to be repositioned after first checking if the path exists in a whitelist of valid static files. The security check was in the wrong order relative to the whitelist validation.

cve_description: In Das U-Boot through 2022.07-rc5, an integer signedness error and resultant stack-based buffer overflow in the "i2c md" command enables the corruption of the return address pointer of the do_i2c_md function.
cause_reason: The initial patch converted variables from signed int to unsigned uint to prevent negative values, but failed to consider that this change could cause integer overflow when variables are used in arithmetic operations or comparisons, leading to stack overflow vulnerabilities.

cve_description: nfs_lookup_reply in net/nfs.c in Das U-Boot through 2022.04 (and through 2022.07-rc2) has an unbounded memcpy with a failed length check, leading to a buffer overflow. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2019-14196.
cause_reason: C1 added bounds checks but missed that negative filefh3_length could bypass the size check. C2 changes to unsigned int.

cve_description: SDL_ttf v2.0.18 and below was discovered to contain an arbitrary memory write via the function TTF_RenderText_Solid(). This vulnerability is triggered via a crafted TTF file.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed integer overflow in three Create_Surface functions (Solid, Shaded, Blended) by adding explicit cast to Sint64, but missed the same vulnerable pattern in the Create_Surface_LCD function. The follow-up patch applies the identical fix to the overlooked LCD variant at the same type of calculation.

cve_description: Multiple race conditions in the ext4 filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel before 4.5 allow local users to cause a denial of service (disk corruption) by writing to a page that is associated with a different user's file after unsynchronized hole punching and page-fault handling.
cause_reason: C1 fixed race in ext4 DAX fault handlers. C2 pushed fix to generic DAX layer affecting ext2 and xfs too.

cve_description: In the Linux kernel before 6.0.3, drivers/gpu/drm/virtio/virtgpu_object.c misinterprets the drm_gem_shmem_get_sg_table return value (expects it to be NULL in the error case, whereas it is actually an error pointer).
cause_reason: C1 fixed IS_ERR check but didn't reset shmem->pages to NULL on error path, leading to use-after-error.

cve_description: The sr_do_ioctl function in drivers/scsi/sr_ioctl.c in the Linux kernel through 4.16.12 allows local users to cause a denial of service (stack-based buffer overflow) or possibly have unspecified other impact because sense buffers have different sizes at the CDROM layer and the SCSI layer, as demonstrated by a CDROMREADMODE2 ioctl call.
cause_reason: The initial patch (C1) fixed the stack overflow vulnerability in sr_ioctl.c by using a local buffer, but the follow-up patch (C2) shows the same issue existed more broadly in the scsi_execute function interface across the entire SCSI subsystem. The C2 patch implements a comprehensive fix by adding compile-time size checking to prevent similar buffer overflows in all callers of scsi_execute.

cve_description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel before 4.20. There is a race condition in smp_task_timedout() and smp_task_done() in drivers/scsi/libsas/sas_expander.c, leading to a use-after-free.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed the race condition in sas_expander.c's smp_task_timedout and smp_task_done functions, but the same vulnerability pattern existed in pm8001_sas.c's pm8001_tmf_timedout and pm8001_task_done functions. The follow-up patch applies identical fixes to these additional code locations that were missed in the original fix.

cve_description: Botan 2.5.0 through 2.6.0 before 2.7.0 allows a memory-cache side-channel attack on ECDSA signatures, aka the Return Of the Hidden Number Problem or ROHNP, related to dsa/dsa.cpp, ec_group/ec_group.cpp, and ecdsa/ecdsa.cpp. To discover an ECDSA key, the attacker needs access to either the local machine or a different virtual machine on the same physical host.
cause_reason: The initial fix (C1) implemented side-channel protection for ECDSA/DSA signatures but missed handling boundary cases in the modular reduction logic. The follow-up fix (C2) addresses the specific edge case where x_sw < m_mod_words - 1, properly handling small values and negative numbers that the original Barrett reduction implementation didn't cover correctly.

cve_description: The mov_read_dref function in libavformat/mov.c in Libav before 11.7 and FFmpeg before 0.11 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) or execute arbitrary code via the entries value in a dref box in an MP4 file.
cause_reason: The initial patch placed `sc->drefs_count = 0` after the validation checks but before the memory allocation, while the follow-up moved it before `av_free(sc->drefs)` to ensure proper state reset regardless of allocation success or failure.

cve_description: An issue was discovered in net/tipc/crypto.c in the Linux kernel before 5.14.16. The Transparent Inter-Process Communication (TIPC) functionality allows remote attackers to exploit insufficient validation of user-supplied sizes for the MSG_CRYPTO message type.
cause_reason: The original fix added size validation for MSG_CRYPTO messages but missed checking the decryption state boundary condition. The follow-up fix adds a check for the `decrypted` flag to prevent processing encrypted messages that should fall through to default handling.

cve_description: The Linux kernel before 3.11 on ARM platforms, as used in Android before 2016-08-05 on Nexus 5 and 7 (2013) devices, does not properly consider user-space access to the TPIDRURW register, which allows local users to gain privileges via a crafted application, aka Android internal bug 28749743 and Qualcomm internal bug CR561044.
cause_reason: The ARM patch correctly implements dual TLS register support but the ARM64 follow-up patch has inconsistent logic in copy_thread() where it reads the current TLS value into task_user_tls(p) for all cases but only updates tp_value for CLONE_SETTLS, creating asymmetric handling of the two TLS storage locations.

cve_description: The cp2112_gpio_direction_input function in drivers/hid/hid-cp2112.c in the Linux kernel 4.9.x before 4.9.9 does not have the expected EIO error status for a zero-length report, which allows local users to have an unspecified impact via unknown vectors.
cause_reason: The original fix changed the condition from `ret <= 0` to `ret < 0` at the return statement, but missed that the boundary value of 0 (and positive values less than expected length) needed proper error handling at the actual validation points where the HID functions return their results.

cve_description: redirect() in bottle.py in bottle 0.12.10 doesn't filter a "\r\n" sequence, which leads to a CRLF attack, as demonstrated by a redirect("233\r\nSet-Cookie: name=salt") call.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed header validation in HeaderDict class methods but missed the same vulnerability in BaseResponse class methods. The follow-up patch applies the same _hval() validation to BaseResponse's header manipulation methods like add_header, set_header, and __setitem__.

cve_description: The cdf_read_short_sector function in cdf.c in file before 5.19, as used in the Fileinfo component in PHP before 5.4.30 and 5.5.x before 5.5.14, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (assertion failure and application exit) via a crafted CDF file.
cause_reason: The original fix added bounds checking but missed the edge case where nelements is 0, which could cause issues in the vector processing loop. The follow-up patch adds specific validation for the zero boundary value that the initial fix overlooked.

cve_description: Sandstorm Cap'n Proto before 0.4.1.1 and 0.5.x before 0.5.1.1 allows remote peers to cause a denial of service (CPU and possibly general resource consumption) via a list with a large number of elements.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed amplification attacks for zero-sized elements but missed the case of nested lists containing zero-sized elements. The follow-up patch shows the fix needed to handle lists-of-lists with empty structs, which is a different input variant of the same amplification vulnerability at the same validation points.

cve_description: The fork implementation in the Linux kernel before 4.5 on s390 platforms mishandles the case of four page-table levels, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted application, related to arch/s390/include/asm/mmu_context.h and arch/s390/include/asm/pgalloc.h.
cause_reason: C1 left empty stubs for arch_dup_mmap/arch_exit_mmap instead of removing them and using generic mm_hooks.h.

cve_description: The xc2028_set_config function in drivers/media/tuners/tuner-xc2028.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) via vectors involving omission of the firmware name from a certain data structure.
cause_reason: The initial patch introduced logic inconsistency by using early return without proper cleanup (missing mutex unlock), which was then corrected by subsequent patches that added proper goto-based cleanup flow and restructured the resource management logic.

cve_description: The IP stack in the Linux kernel before 4.6 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (stack consumption and panic) or possibly have unspecified other impact by triggering use of the GRO path for packets with tunnel stacking, as demonstrated by interleaved IPv4 headers and GRE headers, a related issue to CVE-2016-7039.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed encap_mark handling in several tunnel protocols (IPIP, GRE, SIT, UDP) but missed FOU and GUE protocols. The follow-up patch applies the same encap_mark clearing logic to FOU and GUE receive functions that were overlooked in the initial fix.

cve_description: Redis is an open source, in-memory database that persists on disk. The redis-cli command line tool and redis-sentinel service may be vulnerable to integer overflow when parsing specially crafted large multi-bulk network replies. This is a result of a vulnerability in the underlying hiredis library which does not perform an overflow check before calling the calloc() heap allocation function. This issue only impacts systems with heap allocators that do not perform their own overflow checks. Most modern systems do and are therefore not likely to be affected. Furthermore, by default redis-sentinel uses the jemalloc allocator which is also not vulnerable. The problem is fixed in Redis versions 6.2.6, 6.0.16 and 5.0.14.
cause_reason: The original fix added overflow protection in createArrayObject but missed that the underlying hi_calloc function itself needed the same overflow check. The follow-up fix moves the overflow validation to hi_calloc where it covers all callers, not just the specific case in createArrayObject.

cve_description: net/sctp/socket.c in the Linux kernel through 4.10.1 does not properly restrict association peel-off operations during certain wait states, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (invalid unlock and double free) via a multithreaded application.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2017-5986.
cause_reason: The original fix missed the exceptional state where the socket can change during the wait period due to peeloff operations. The follow-up patch handles this by tracking socket changes and updating the reference accordingly.

cve_description: The trace_writeback_dirty_page implementation in include/trace/events/writeback.h in the Linux kernel before 4.4 improperly interacts with mm/migrate.c, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact by triggering a certain page move.
cause_reason: The original patch correctly moved dirty page handling to migrate_page_move_mapping() and simplified migrate_page_copy(), but the follow-up changes in exofs and nfs objlayout removed the logic that considered PageDirty() pages as uptodate, creating inconsistent page state handling across the migration process.

cve_description: Use-after-free vulnerability in the ff_h264_free_tables function in libavcodec/h264.c in FFmpeg before 2.3.6 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted H.264 data in an MP4 file, as demonstrated by an HTML VIDEO element that references H.264 data.
cause_reason: The initial fix cleared delayed_pic array but missed that context_initialized flag needed to be reset when reinitializing, leaving the decoder in an inconsistent state during reinitialization scenarios.

cve_description: arch/x86/kernel/tls.c in the Thread Local Storage (TLS) implementation in the Linux kernel through 3.18.1 allows local users to bypass the espfix protection mechanism, and consequently makes it easier for local users to bypass the ASLR protection mechanism, via a crafted application that makes a set_thread_area system call and later reads a 16-bit value.
cause_reason: The original patch was overly strict by rejecting all non-32-bit segments, but it failed to account for zero-filled user_desc structures that programs expect to mean 'no segment at all'. The follow-up patch adds the LDT_zero() check to properly handle this common case that should be allowed.

cve_description: The join_session_keyring function in security/keys/process_keys.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4.1 mishandles object references in a certain error case, which allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (integer overflow and use-after-free) via crafted keyctl commands.
cause_reason: The initial fix added key_put() in the wrong location, causing resource management issues. The follow-up fix moved the key_put() to a proper cleanup label to handle the exceptional state where the keyring needs to be released consistently across different error paths.

cve_description: The Linux kernel 4.x (starting from 4.1) and 5.x before 5.0.8 allows Information Exposure (partial kernel address disclosure), leading to a KASLR bypass. Specifically, it is possible to extract the KASLR kernel image offset using the IP ID values the kernel produces for connection-less protocols (e.g., UDP and ICMP). When such traffic is sent to multiple destination IP addresses, it is possible to obtain hash collisions (of indices to the counter array) and thereby obtain the hashing key (via enumeration). This key contains enough bits from a kernel address (of a static variable) so when the key is extracted (via enumeration), the offset of the kernel image is exposed. This attack can be carried out remotely, by the attacker forcing the target device to send UDP or ICMP (or certain other) traffic to attacker-controlled IP addresses. Forcing a server to send UDP traffic is trivial if the server is a DNS server. ICMP traffic is trivial if the server answers ICMP Echo requests (ping). For client targets, if the target visits the attacker's web page, then WebRTC or gQUIC can be used to force UDP traffic to attacker-controlled IP addresses. NOTE: this attack against KASLR became viable in 4.1 because IP ID generation was changed to have a dependency on an address associated with a network namespace.
cause_reason: The initial patch placed the hash_mix field in a frequently dirtied cache line, causing performance issues. The follow-up fix moved hash_mix to a read-mostly cache line with proper documentation, showing the original placement logic was flawed.

cve_description: An array overflow was discovered in mt76_add_fragment in drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/dma.c in the Linux kernel before 5.5.10, aka CID-b102f0c522cf. An oversized packet with too many rx fragments can corrupt memory of adjacent pages.
cause_reason: The initial patch only added a bounds check to prevent adding fragments when the array is full, but failed to handle the memory leak case where data is not freed when fragments can't be added. The follow-up patches show the original fix had inconsistent logic by not properly handling all code paths.

cve_description: There is a flaw in RPM's signature functionality. OpenPGP subkeys are associated with a primary key via a "binding signature." RPM does not check the binding signature of subkeys prior to importing them. If an attacker is able to add or socially engineer another party to add a malicious subkey to a legitimate public key, RPM could wrongly trust a malicious signature. The greatest impact of this flaw is to data integrity. To exploit this flaw, an attacker must either compromise an RPM repository or convince an administrator to install an untrusted RPM or public key. It is strongly recommended to only use RPMs and public keys from trusted sources.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed memory leak in pgpPrtParams but missed a similar resource management issue in haveSignature function where pgpDigParamsFree was called without assigning the return value back to the pointer.

cve_description: Multiple integer overflows in the lzo1x_decompress_safe function in lib/lzo/lzo1x_decompress_safe.c in the LZO decompressor in the Linux kernel before 3.15.2 allow context-dependent attackers to cause a denial of service (memory corruption) via a crafted Literal Run.  NOTE: the author of the LZO algorithms says "the Linux kernel is *not* affected; media hype.
cause_reason: The original fix (C1) added overflow protection for the addition operation (t + x) but missed the critical boundary check for the loop counter that accumulates 255 values. C2 adds a MAX_255_COUNT boundary check to prevent integer overflow when too many consecutive 255 bytes are processed in the same validation loops.

cve_description: Integer overflow in the read_fragment_table_4 function in unsquash-4.c in Squashfs and sasquatch allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted input, which triggers a stack-based buffer overflow.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed integer overflow vulnerabilities in squashfs-tools version 4 code paths, but the follow-up patches show the same types of vulnerabilities existed in the version 2 and 3 code paths (unsquash-2.c and unsquash-3.c) which weren't addressed in the original fix.

cve_description: fs/pipe.c in the Linux kernel before 4.5 does not limit the amount of unread data in pipes, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by creating many pipes with non-default sizes.
cause_reason: The original patch failed to check if the user is unprivileged before applying pipe buffer limits, causing the limits to incorrectly apply to privileged users who should be exempt. The fix adds proper privilege checks to ensure only unprivileged users are subject to the buffer restrictions.

cve_description: qfq_change_class in net/sched/sch_qfq.c in the Linux kernel before 6.2.13 allows an out-of-bounds write because lmax can exceed QFQ_MIN_LMAX.
cause_reason: The original fix moved validation from only user-provided lmax to all lmax values, but missed that MTU-derived lmax could exceed QFQ_MAX_LMAX. The follow-up adds the missing upper bound check for MTU values that the original validation didn't cover.

cve_description: A heap-based buffer overflow issue was discovered in libjpeg-turbo in h2v2_merged_upsample_internal() function of jdmrgext.c file. The vulnerability can only be exploited with 12-bit data precision for which the range of the sample data type exceeds the valid sample range, hence, an attacker could craft a 12-bit lossless JPEG image that contains out-of-range 12-bit samples. An application attempting to decompress such image using merged upsampling would lead to segmentation fault or buffer overflows, causing an application to crash.
cause_reason: The initial patch added range-limiting to prevent out-of-range values from being used as array indices, but the follow-up evidence shows this approach was flawed. The real issue was that color quantization and merged upsampling algorithms were incorrectly enabled for lossless JPEG images, so the proper fix was to disable these incompatible features entirely rather than just range-limiting the values.

cve_description: Heap-based Buffer Overflow in GitHub repository gpac/gpac prior to v2.3.0-DEV.
cause_reason: The original fix added a size check but used a simple return, missing the exceptional state where resources need cleanup. The follow-up fix replaces the return with goto error_exit to properly handle resource cleanup in the error condition.

cve_description: arch/x86/kvm/emulate.c in the Linux kernel through 4.9.3 allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) via a crafted application that leverages instruction emulation for fxrstor, fxsave, sgdt, and sidt.
cause_reason: The initial fix added segmented_write_std() for user-level memory operations but overlooked system-level memory operations that also needed protection. The follow-up adds linear_read_system() and linear_write_system() to handle the exceptional case of system-level descriptor table and TSS operations.

cve_description: A use-after-free flaw was found in fs/userfaultfd.c in the Linux kernel before 4.13.6. The issue is related to the handling of fork failure when dealing with event messages. Failure to fork correctly can lead to a situation where a fork event will be removed from an already freed list of events with userfaultfd_ctx_put().
cause_reason: The original patch (C1) fixed reference counting and race conditions but missed handling the exceptional state where the fork thread aborts and releases its reference, leaving VMA structures still pointing to the freed context. The follow-up patch (C2) addresses this overlooked state by properly cleaning up VMA references when the context is being released.

cve_description: Integer overflow in the snd_compr_allocate_buffer function in sound/core/compress_offload.c in the ALSA subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.6-rc6-next-20120917 allows local users to cause a denial of service (insufficient memory allocation) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted SNDRV_COMPRESS_SET_PARAMS ioctl call.
cause_reason: The original fix used SIZE_MAX as the overflow threshold, but the follow-up patch changed it to INT_MAX, indicating the original boundary value was incorrect for preventing integer overflow in this specific context.

cve_description: The ioapic_read_indirect function in virt/kvm/ioapic.c in the Linux kernel through 3.8.4 does not properly handle a certain combination of invalid IOAPIC_REG_SELECT and IOAPIC_REG_WINDOW operations, which allows guest OS users to obtain sensitive information from host OS memory or cause a denial of service (host OS OOPS) via a crafted application.
cause_reason: The original patch (C1) fixed bounds checking in the IOAPIC read function, but the follow-up patch (C2) reveals that speculative execution attacks were not considered, requiring additional mitigation with array_index_nospec() to prevent potential side-channel vulnerabilities in the same code path.

cve_description: Multiple integer overflows in Alchemy LCD frame-buffer drivers in the Linux kernel before 3.12 allow local users to create a read-write memory mapping for the entirety of kernel memory, and consequently gain privileges, via crafted mmap operations, related to the (1) au1100fb_fb_mmap function in drivers/video/au1100fb.c and the (2) au1200fb_fb_mmap function in drivers/video/au1200fb.c.
cause_reason: The original fix added a size check but missed validating that the memory address is page-aligned. The follow-up adds a check for the specific boundary condition where mem->addr is not aligned to PAGE_MASK at the same validation point.

cve_description: The Btrfs implementation in the Linux kernel before 3.19 does not ensure that the visible xattr state is consistent with a requested replacement, which allows local users to bypass intended ACL settings and gain privileges via standard filesystem operations (1) during an xattr-replacement time window, related to a race condition, or (2) after an xattr-replacement attempt that fails because the data does not fit.
cause_reason: The initial patch added error handling for the btrfs_lookup_xattr function in one code path but missed handling IS_ERR cases in two other locations within the same function. The follow-up patch adds the missing IS_ERR checks for the same function calls in different conditional branches.

cve_description: A Reachable Assertion issue was discovered in the KDC in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) before 1.17. If an attacker can obtain a krbtgt ticket using an older encryption type (single-DES, triple-DES, or RC4), the attacker can crash the KDC by making an S4U2Self request.
cause_reason: The original fix in C1 handled password expiration issues for S4U2Self requests but missed that the assertion `assert(reply_encpart->enc_padata == NULL)` could fail when S4U2Self processing was involved. C2 removes this assertion that was triggering in the exceptional state where enc_padata was already set during S4U2Self flows.

cve_description: The KVM subsystem in the Linux kernel through 3.12.5 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (system crash) via a VAPIC synchronization operation involving a page-end address.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed the race condition by replacing direct memory mapping with cached guest reads/writes, but missed that the vapic_cache initialization itself needed SRCU protection when accessing guest memory structures.

cve_description: The mISDN_sock_recvmsg function in drivers/isdn/mISDN/socket.c in the Linux kernel before 3.12.4 does not ensure that a certain length value is consistent with the size of an associated data structure, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel memory via a (1) recvfrom, (2) recvmmsg, or (3) recvmsg system call.
cause_reason: The initial patch (C1) systematically removed msg_namelen initialization from many socket protocols but missed the ROSE protocol's recvmsg implementation. The follow-up patch (C2) shows fixes were needed in additional locations like net/rose/af_rose.c and other protocol handlers that weren't covered in the original comprehensive patch.

cve_description: Heap-based buffer overflow in the php_parserr function in ext/standard/dns.c in PHP 5.6.0beta4 and earlier allows remote servers to cause a denial of service (crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via a crafted DNS TXT record, related to the dns_get_record function.
cause_reason: The original fix only added a bounds check for chunk length in the TXT record parsing loop, but missed comprehensive bounds checking throughout the DNS parsing function for all data access operations. The follow-up fix adds systematic CHECKCP boundary checks at every point where data is read from the DNS response buffer.

cve_description: The inode_init_owner function in fs/inode.c in the Linux kernel through 3.16 allows local users to create files with an unintended group ownership, in a scenario where a directory is SGID to a certain group and is writable by a user who is not a member of that group. Here, the non-member can trigger creation of a plain file whose group ownership is that group. The intended behavior was that the non-member can trigger creation of a directory (but not a plain file) whose group ownership is that group. The non-member can escalate privileges by making the plain file executable and SGID.
cause_reason: The original fix in inode.c handled setgid bit inheritance for general inode creation, but missed the ceph filesystem's async file creation path which has its own separate implementation of the same logic.

cve_description: Race condition in the ssl3_get_new_session_ticket function in ssl/s3_clnt.c in OpenSSL before 0.9.8zg, 1.0.0 before 1.0.0s, 1.0.1 before 1.0.1n, and 1.0.2 before 1.0.2b, when used for a multi-threaded client, allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (double free and application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact by providing a NewSessionTicket during an attempt to reuse a ticket that had been obtained earlier.
cause_reason: The original fix created a ssl_session_dup function but failed to properly initialize pointer fields to NULL before attempting allocations, creating a race condition where SSL_SESSION_free could be called on uninitialized pointers if allocation failed partway through. The follow-up fix addresses this by explicitly setting all pointer fields to NULL upfront to ensure safe cleanup in error conditions.

cve_description: The dgram_recvmsg function in net/ieee802154/dgram.c in the Linux kernel before 3.12.4 updates a certain length value without ensuring that an associated data structure has been initialized, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from kernel stack memory via a (1) recvfrom, (2) recvmmsg, or (3) recvmsg system call.
cause_reason: The initial patch (C1) fixed address length handling in multiple networking protocol functions, but missed the l2tp_ip6_recvmsg function. The follow-up patch (C2) applies the same fix pattern to the missed l2tp_ip6 code path, moving addr_len assignment inside the conditional block where the address is actually populated.

cve_description: An issue was discovered in the Linux kernel through 4.18.8. The vmacache_flush_all function in mm/vmacache.c mishandles sequence number overflows. An attacker can trigger a use-after-free (and possibly gain privileges) via certain thread creation, map, unmap, invalidation, and dereference operations.
cause_reason: The original implementation had flawed overflow handling logic that attempted to flush all vmacaches when the 32-bit sequence number wrapped around, but this approach was fundamentally broken and could cause race conditions. The fix resolves this by expanding to 64-bit sequence numbers, eliminating the need for overflow handling entirely.

cve_description: Mutt before 1.14.3 allows an IMAP fcc/postpone man-in-the-middle attack via a PREAUTH response.
cause_reason: The initial patch was overly strict by blocking all unencrypted PREAUTH connections, but the fix shows it should allow connections when using tunnels (!Tunnel condition added). The original condition was too restrictive and blocked valid tunnel-based connections.

cve_description: The disas_insn function in target/i386/translate.c in QEMU before 2.9.0, when TCG mode without hardware acceleration is used, does not limit the instruction size, which allows local users to gain privileges by creating a modified basic block that injects code into a setuid program, as demonstrated by procmail. NOTE: the vendor has stated "this bug does not violate any security guarantees QEMU makes.
cause_reason: The original fix used a limit of 14 bytes but failed to account for the precise x86 instruction length limit of 15 bytes. The follow-up fix corrects this by using the proper X86_MAX_INSN_LENGTH constant of 15 bytes and handles the edge case where the 16th byte might trigger a page fault.

cve_description: The BGP parser in tcpdump before 4.9.3 allows stack consumption in print-bgp.c:bgp_attr_print() because of unlimited recursion.
cause_reason: The original fix implemented recursion depth limiting for ATTR_SET attributes but missed handling the exact boundary case where attr_set_level equals 10. The follow-up fix corrected this by properly checking the boundary condition and handling the case where the recursion limit is reached.

cve_description: fs/seq_file.c in the Linux kernel 3.16 through 5.13.x before 5.13.4 does not properly restrict seq buffer allocations, leading to an integer overflow, an Out-of-bounds Write, and escalation to root by an unprivileged user, aka CID-8cae8cd89f05.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed buffer size validation in seq_file.c to prevent stack overflow, but the follow-up diff shows similar memory safety issues in kmemleak.c where KASAN tag handling was missing in multiple functions that access memory pointers.

cve_description: The sysrq_sysctl_handler function in kernel/sysctl.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39 does not require the CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability to modify the dmesg_restrict value, which allows local users to bypass intended access restrictions and read the kernel ring buffer by leveraging root privileges, as demonstrated by a root user in a Linux Containers (aka LXC) environment.
cause_reason: C1 applied CAP_SYS_ADMIN check only to kptr_restrict instead of both dmesg_restrict and kptr_restrict.

cve_description: The ext4_fill_flex_info function in fs/ext4/super.c in the Linux kernel before 3.2.2, on the x86 platform and unspecified other platforms, allows user-assisted remote attackers to trigger inconsistent filesystem-groups data and possibly cause a denial of service via a malformed ext4 filesystem containing a super block with a large FLEX_BG group size (aka s_log_groups_per_flex value).  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2009-4307.
cause_reason: The original fix changed the variable type to unsigned int and added bounds checking for s_log_groups_per_flex, but missed that the bit shift operation itself needed to use an unsigned literal (1U) to prevent signed integer overflow when shifting reaches the upper bounds of the valid range.

cve_description: mm/memory.c in the Linux kernel before 4.1.4 mishandles anonymous pages, which allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (page tainting) via a crafted application that triggers writing to page zero.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed memory handling issues in the memory management code but missed updating the MPX (Memory Protection Extensions) implementation which had its own VMA operations and identification mechanism. The follow-up patch shows that MPX code needed similar fixes to handle VMAs consistently with the updated memory management logic.

cve_description: Endless recursion when handling responses from an IAS-ECC card in iasecc_select_file in libopensc/card-iasecc.c in OpenSC before 0.19.0-rc1 could be used by attackers able to supply crafted smartcards to hang or crash the opensc library using programs.
cause_reason: The initial patch added a condition to check path type but the follow-up patch shows it missed considering a different card type scenario (CPX cards) that required an additional condition check. The fix was applied to the general case but missed the specific card type variant that needed different handling.

cve_description: Vyper is a Pythonic programming language that targets the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). Prior to version 0.3.10, the ecrecover precompile does not fill the output buffer if the signature does not verify. However, the ecrecover builtin will still return whatever is at memory location 0. This means that the if the compiler has been convinced to write to the 0 memory location with specially crafted data (generally, this can happen with a hashmap access or immutable read) just before the ecrecover, a signature check might pass on an invalid signature. Version 0.3.10 contains a patch for this issue.
cause_reason: The original patch cleared the output buffer at a fixed memory location but missed that intermediate operations during ecrecover execution could overwrite that same memory location. The follow-up fix allocates a dedicated output buffer to handle the exceptional state where memory gets stomped during builtin execution.

cve_description: Use-after-free vulnerability in net/unix/af_unix.c in the Linux kernel before 4.3.3 allows local users to bypass intended AF_UNIX socket permissions or cause a denial of service (panic) via crafted epoll_ctl calls.
cause_reason: The original fix missed the exceptional state where `other == sk` (self-connection case), which can occur when unix_peer(sk) == NULL or becomes disconnected before acquiring locks. The follow-up patches add explicit checks for this self-reference edge case that the original implementation didn't handle.

cve_description: Integer overflow in the vma_to_resize function in mm/mremap.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39 allows local users to cause a denial of service (BUG_ON and system crash) via a crafted mremap system call that expands a memory mapping.
cause_reason: The original fix (C1) added overflow protection for mremap operations but missed the same overflow vulnerability in the stack expansion code path. C2 adds the missing boundary check for vm_pgoff underflow in expand_downwards at a similar validation point.

cve_description: The Linux kernel before 4.4.1 allows local users to bypass file-descriptor limits and cause a denial of service (memory consumption) by sending each descriptor over a UNIX socket before closing it, related to net/unix/af_unix.c and net/unix/garbage.c.
cause_reason: The initial patch incorrectly used fp->f_cred->user to track unix_inflight counts, but the follow-up fix shows this was wrong because it should use the user from the scm_fp_list structure instead. The patch was using the wrong user pointer for accounting.

cve_description: In net/socket.c in the Linux kernel through 4.17.1, there is a race condition between fchownat and close in cases where they target the same socket file descriptor, related to the sock_close and sockfs_setattr functions. fchownat does not increment the file descriptor reference count, which allows close to set the socket to NULL during fchownat's execution, leading to a NULL pointer dereference and system crash.
cause_reason: The initial patch added null checks and locking but failed to handle the race condition properly where sock->sk could become null between the check and usage. The follow-up patch reveals the inconsistent logic by explicitly setting sock->sk to NULL after releasing it, showing the original fix didn't account for this state change.

cve_description: The journal_unmap_buffer function in fs/jbd2/transaction.c in the Linux kernel before 3.3.1 does not properly handle the _Delay and _Unwritten buffer head states, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) by leveraging the presence of an ext4 filesystem that was mounted with a journal.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed buffer state clearing in journal_unmap_buffer but the follow-up reveals inconsistent truncation logic in ext4_truncate, where page-based partial buffer discard was replaced with block-based truncation, indicating flawed coordination between the journal and filesystem layers.

cve_description: kernel/signal.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39 allows local users to spoof the uid and pid of a signal sender via a sigqueueinfo system call.
cause_reason: The initial fix only allowed SI_QUEUE but missed that SI_TKILL is another legitimate user-space signal code that should also be blocked from impersonation. The follow-up patch adds SI_TKILL to the blocked codes, showing the original fix was too narrow in considering signal code variants.

cve_description: In the Linux kernel before 4.20.2, kernel/sched/fair.c mishandles leaf cfs_rq's, which allows attackers to cause a denial of service (infinite loop in update_blocked_averages) or possibly have unspecified other impact by inducing a high load.
cause_reason: The patch removed the safe iteration mechanism and decayed CFS runqueue cleanup logic, but the follow-up evidence shows this broke list integrity during concurrent modifications. The original logic was correct but the patch incorrectly simplified the iteration without considering race conditions that could corrupt the list structure.

cve_description: Buffer overflow in the fuse_do_ioctl function in fs/fuse/file.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.37 allows local users to cause a denial of service or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging the ability to operate a CUSE server.
cause_reason: The original patch added validation logic but placed it in the wrong location within the loop structure. The follow-up fix shows the validation was checking the same iovec entry repeatedly instead of iterating through all entries due to missing pointer increment.

cve_description: Memory leak in the inotify_init1 function in fs/notify/inotify/inotify_user.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.37 allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via vectors involving failed attempts to create files.
cause_reason: The initial patch added fsnotify_put_group() to one error path but missed that the resource lifecycle management (atomic_dec and free_uid) was incorrectly handled across multiple code paths. The follow-up patch shows the proper fix moved this cleanup into the group destruction function to handle all scenarios consistently.

cve_description: The Reliable Datagram Sockets (RDS) subsystem in the Linux kernel before 2.6.38 does not properly handle congestion map updates, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (BUG_ON and system crash) via vectors involving (1) a loopback (aka loop) transmit operation or (2) an InfiniBand (aka ib) transmit operation.
cause_reason: The original fix used min_t() to prevent exceeding buffer boundaries, but the follow-up shows this was incorrect - it should use max_t() instead. The fix missed the proper boundary calculation for the congestion map size relative to scatter-gather buffer length.

cve_description: Race condition in arch/x86/kvm/x86.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.38 allows L2 guest OS users to cause a denial of service (L1 guest OS crash) via a crafted instruction that triggers an L2 emulation failure report, a similar issue to CVE-2014-7842.
cause_reason: The initial patch only checked if the vcpu is in guest mode, but the follow-up patch shows this wasn't sufficient - it needed an additional check for privilege level (CPL == 0) to properly handle all emulation failure scenarios.

cve_description: Format string vulnerability in the yyerror function in lib/cgraph/scan.l in Graphviz allows remote attackers to have unspecified impact via format string specifiers in unknown vectors, which are not properly handled in an error string.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed a format string vulnerability in one function (yyerror in scan.l) by adding '%s' format specifier, but the same vulnerability existed in multiple other functions and files that also called agerr() with user-controlled strings directly as format strings.

cve_description: arch/x86/kvm/x86.c in the Linux kernel before 4.4 does not reset the PIT counter values during state restoration, which allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (divide-by-zero error and host OS crash) via a zero value, related to the kvm_vm_ioctl_set_pit and kvm_vm_ioctl_set_pit2 functions.
cause_reason: The original fix correctly expanded the loop to handle all 3 PIT channels but missed that the hpet_legacy_start parameter should only apply to channel 0. The follow-up fix adds a WARN_ON check and corrects the logic to only pass the start parameter when i==0, handling the exceptional state where legacy HPET mode is incorrectly applied to non-zero channels.

cve_description: The inet_csk_clone_lock function in net/ipv4/inet_connection_sock.c in the Linux kernel through 4.10.15 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (double free) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging use of the accept system call.
cause_reason: The initial patch only fixed the double free issue for IPv4 multicast lists in inet_connection_sock.c, but the same vulnerability existed in IPv6 code paths for DCCP and TCP protocols, requiring additional fixes to properly initialize IPv6 multicast, anycast, and flow label lists.

cve_description: hb-ot-layout-gsubgpos.hh in HarfBuzz through 6.0.0 allows attackers to trigger O(n^2) growth via consecutive marks during the process of looking back for base glyphs when attaching marks.
cause_reason: The original fix added a search limit to prevent O(n^2) behavior but overlooked edge cases where this optimization caused incorrect results in certain buffer states. The follow-up patch reverts the optimization and implements a more sophisticated approach that handles different cluster configurations and edge cases properly.

cve_description: Waitress is a Web Server Gateway Interface server for Python 2 and 3. When using Waitress versions 2.1.0 and prior behind a proxy that does not properly validate the incoming HTTP request matches the RFC7230 standard, Waitress and the frontend proxy may disagree on where one request starts and where it ends. This would allow requests to be smuggled via the front-end proxy to waitress and later behavior. There are two classes of vulnerability that may lead to request smuggling that are addressed by this advisory: The use of Python's `int()` to parse strings into integers, leading to `+10` to be parsed as `10`, or `0x01` to be parsed as `1`, where as the standard specifies that the string should contain only digits or hex digits; and Waitress does not support chunk extensions, however it was discarding them without validating that they did not contain illegal characters. This vulnerability has been patched in Waitress 2.1.1. A workaround is available. When deploying a proxy in front of waitress, turning on any and all functionality to make sure that the request matches the RFC7230 standard. Certain proxy servers may not have this functionality though and users are encouraged to upgrade to the latest version of waitress instead.
cause_reason: The initial patch (C1) fixed HTTP request smuggling vulnerabilities by validating chunked encoding and Content-Length headers, but missed a related configuration issue where clear_untrusted_proxy_headers defaulted to True in the security fix but should have remained False to maintain backward compatibility. The follow-up patch (C2) addresses this oversight by reverting the default value and adding proper deprecation warnings.

cve_description: Armeria is an open source microservice framework. In affected versions an attacker can access an Armeria server's local file system beyond its restricted directory by sending an HTTP request whose path contains `%2F` (encoded `/`), such as `/files/..%2Fsecrets.txt`, bypassing Armeria's path validation logic. Armeria 1.13.4 or above contains the hardened path validation logic that handles `%2F` properly. This vulnerability can be worked around by inserting a decorator that performs an additional validation on the request path.
cause_reason: The original code was too restrictive by always rejecting double dots (..) in query strings, even when they might be safe. The fix introduces a flag to allow double dots in query strings when specifically configured, changing from an overly strict blanket prohibition to a more nuanced approach that considers security context.

cve_description: net/nfc/llcp_sock.c in the Linux kernel before 5.12.10 allows local unprivileged users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and BUG) by making a getsockname call after a certain type of failure of a bind call.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed null pointer issues in the llcp_sock_bind function by setting llcp_sock->dev = NULL in error paths, but missed the same vulnerability in the llcp_sock_connect function which also needed the same fix.

cve_description: A flaw was found in the KVM's AMD code for supporting SVM nested virtualization. The flaw occurs when processing the VMCB (virtual machine control block) provided by the L1 guest to spawn/handle a nested guest (L2). Due to improper validation of the "virt_ext" field, this issue could allow a malicious L1 to disable both VMLOAD/VMSAVE intercepts and VLS (Virtual VMLOAD/VMSAVE) for the L2 guest. As a result, the L2 guest would be allowed to read/write physical pages of the host, resulting in a crash of the entire system, leak of sensitive data or potential guest-to-host escape.
cause_reason: C1 forced VMLOAD/VMSAVE intercepts but didn't prevent guest from enabling virtual VMLOAD/VMSAVE to bypass intercepts.

cve_description: An error in the implementation of an autosubscribe feature in the check_stream_exists route of the Zulip group chat application server before 1.4.3 allowed an authenticated user to subscribe to a private stream that should have required an invitation from an existing member to join. The issue affects all previously released versions of the Zulip server.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed the autosubscribe vulnerability in the stream_exists_backend function but missed implementing proper access control mechanisms for private streams throughout the codebase. The follow-up patch introduces comprehensive access_stream_by_* functions to handle stream access validation across different code paths.

cve_description: The mincore() implementation in mm/mincore.c in the Linux kernel through 4.19.13 allowed local attackers to observe page cache access patterns of other processes on the same system, potentially allowing sniffing of secret information. (Fixing this affects the output of the fincore program.) Limited remote exploitation may be possible, as demonstrated by latency differences in accessing public files from an Apache HTTP Server.
cause_reason: The original patch simplified mincore to always return 0 for unmapped ranges and use basic swap entry detection, but missed the exceptional state where file-backed mappings need proper page cache lookup to determine if pages are actually present in memory versus just mapped.

cve_description: User after free in mrb_vm_exec in GitHub repository mruby/mruby prior to 3.2.
cause_reason: The original patch fixed register assignment issues for several VM opcodes but missed the same pattern in OP_RANGE_INC and OP_RANGE_EXC opcodes. The follow-up patches show identical fixes being applied to these additional opcodes that handle range creation, indicating the same vulnerability pattern existed in multiple input variants at the VM instruction level.

cve_description: A temp directory creation vulnerability exists in all versions of Guava, allowing an attacker with access to the machine to potentially access data in a temporary directory created by the Guava API com.google.common.io.Files.createTempDir(). By default, on unix-like systems, the created directory is world-readable (readable by an attacker with access to the system). The method in question has been marked @Deprecated in versions 30.0 and later and should not be used. For Android developers, we recommend choosing a temporary directory API provided by Android, such as context.getCacheDir(). For other Java developers, we recommend migrating to the Java 7 API java.nio.file.Files.createTempDirectory() which explicitly configures permissions of 700, or configuring the Java runtime's java.io.tmpdir system property to point to a location whose permissions are appropriately configured.
cause_reason: The initial patch only added documentation warnings about security risks but failed to implement the actual security fix to restrict file permissions. The complete fix required implementing a new TempFileCreator system with proper permission restrictions, showing the original patch had insufficient logic to address the vulnerability.

cve_description: mm/filemap.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.25 allows local users to cause a denial of service (infinite loop) via a writev system call that triggers an iovec of zero length, followed by a page fault for an iovec of nonzero length.
cause_reason: The iov_iter_advance() call was positioned after the zero-copy check, causing the iterator to advance even when no data was actually copied. Moving it before the check ensures the iterator only advances when data is successfully copied.

cve_description: drivers/acpi/debugfs.c in the Linux kernel before 3.0 allows local users to modify arbitrary kernel memory locations by leveraging root privileges to write to the /sys/kernel/debug/acpi/custom_method file. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2010-4347.
cause_reason: The original patch has inconsistent memory management logic where the buffer is freed in some error paths but not in others, and the buffer is not properly reset to NULL after being freed at function completion. The follow-up patches fix these logical inconsistencies by adding missing kfree() calls and proper buffer management.

cve_description: Buffer overflow in the macvtap device driver in the Linux kernel before 3.4.5, when running in certain configurations, allows privileged KVM guest users to cause a denial of service (crash) via a long descriptor with a long vector length.
cause_reason: The original patch added a check for `i + size > MAX_SKB_FRAGS` but missed the boundary case where the total page count across all iovec segments could still exceed MAX_SKB_FRAGS. The follow-up fix adds the `iov_pages()` function to properly calculate and validate the total page count before enabling zero-copy mode.

cve_description: The sock_setsockopt function in net/core/sock.c in the Linux kernel before 3.5 mishandles negative values of sk_sndbuf and sk_rcvbuf, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (memory corruption and system crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact by leveraging the CAP_NET_ADMIN capability for a crafted setsockopt system call with the (1) SO_SNDBUF or (2) SO_RCVBUF option.
cause_reason: The original fix used `max_t(u32, val * 2, SOCK_MIN_SNDBUF)` but missed that `val * 2` could overflow when `val` is a large unsigned 32-bit value, requiring the follow-up to change the type from `u32` to `int` to handle the overflow boundary condition.

cve_description: The recalculate_apic_map function in arch/x86/kvm/lapic.c in the KVM subsystem in the Linux kernel through 3.12.5 allows guest OS users to cause a denial of service (host OS crash) via a crafted ICR write operation in x2apic mode.
cause_reason: The original patch set KVM_X2APIC_CID_BITS to 0, making cid_mask equal to 0 (since (1 << 0) - 1 = 0), which broke the cluster ID calculation logic. The follow-up fix removed this inconsistent logic and restored the proper mask value of 0xffff while adding bounds checking to prevent array access violations.

cve_description: FileSystemBytecodeCache in Jinja2 2.7.2 does not properly create temporary directories, which allows local users to gain privileges by pre-creating a temporary directory with a user's uid.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2014-1402.
cause_reason: The initial patch incorrectly used 'n' instead of 'nt' for Windows OS name detection, causing the security protection to fail on Windows systems. This wrong constant value meant Windows systems would incorrectly take the UNIX code path, potentially creating insecure cache directories.

cve_description: The ndisc_router_discovery function in net/ipv6/ndisc.c in the Neighbor Discovery (ND) protocol implementation in the IPv6 stack in the Linux kernel before 3.19.6 allows remote attackers to reconfigure a hop-limit setting via a small hop_limit value in a Router Advertisement (RA) message.
cause_reason: The original patch implemented flawed logic by only allowing hop limit increases, but the follow-up patch shows this was insufficient and replaced it with a configurable minimum threshold approach, indicating the initial comparison logic was fundamentally incorrect for the security requirements.

cve_description: The sctp_init function in net/sctp/protocol.c in the Linux kernel before 4.2.3 has an incorrect sequence of protocol-initialization steps, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (panic or memory corruption) by creating SCTP sockets before all of the steps have finished.
cause_reason: C1 split SCTP pernet ops but annotated sctp_ctrlsock_exit as __net_init instead of __net_exit.

cve_description: HarfBuzz before 1.0.4 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (invalid read of two bytes and application crash) because of GPOS and GSUB table mishandling, related to hb-ot-layout-gpos-table.hh, hb-ot-layout-gsub-table.hh, and hb-ot-layout-gsubgpos-private.hh.
cause_reason: The initial fix only addressed the return statement syntax but missed that dispatch failure scenarios should return different values than normal default cases. The follow-up fix introduces `no_dispatch_return_value()` to properly handle the exceptional state when dispatch validation fails.

cve_description: BitlBee before 3.5 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference and crash) and possibly execute arbitrary code via a file transfer request for a contact that is not in the contact list.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed the null pointer dereference in bee_ft.c by checking if `bu` is null before using it, but the same vulnerability existed in a different file (protocols/purple/ft.c) where the return value of `imcb_file_send_start` wasn't checked for null before dereferencing `px->ft`.

cve_description: Race condition in the L2TPv3 IP Encapsulation feature in the Linux kernel before 4.8.14 allows local users to gain privileges or cause a denial of service (use-after-free) by making multiple bind system calls without properly ascertaining whether a socket has the SOCK_ZAPPED status, related to net/l2tp/l2tp_ip.c and net/l2tp/l2tp_ip6.c.
cause_reason: The original patch (C1) moved the SOCK_ZAPPED check inside the socket lock but missed race conditions where another thread could perform duplicate bind lookups. The follow-up patch (C2) addresses this by moving the bind lookup check inside the write lock to prevent concurrent access during the critical section.

cve_description: The ext4_fill_super function in fs/ext4/super.c in the Linux kernel through 4.9.8 does not properly validate meta block groups, which allows physically proximate attackers to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and system crash) via a crafted ext4 image.
cause_reason: The original patch used '>=' to check if s_first_meta_bg is greater than or equal to db_count, but the follow-up changed it to '>' indicating the boundary condition was off by one. This is a classic off-by-one error where the equality case was incorrectly included in the invalid range.

cve_description: ext/wddx/wddx.c in PHP before 5.6.28 and 7.x before 7.0.13 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) via crafted serialized data in a wddxPacket XML document, as demonstrated by a PDORow string.
cause_reason: The original fix missed handling cases where deserialization checks should also prevent NULL pointer dereference when the class entry is not found or when ent2->data becomes NULL. The follow-up fix adds proper NULL state handling by setting ZVAL_UNDEF and preventing object initialization when classes cannot be unserialized.

cve_description: Double free vulnerability in MIT Kerberos 5 (aka krb5) allows attackers to have unspecified impact via vectors involving automatic deletion of security contexts on error.
cause_reason: The patch adds checks for GSS_C_NO_CONTEXT at the beginning of many functions, but the original code was performing operations on invalid context handles without validating them first. The checks needed to be placed earlier in the execution flow before attempting to use the context handles.

cve_description: fs/ext4/inode.c in the Linux kernel before 4.6.2, when ext4 data=ordered mode is used, mishandles a needs-flushing-before-commit list, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information from other users' files in opportunistic circumstances by waiting for a hardware reset, creating a new file, making write system calls, and reading this file.
cause_reason: The original fix in C1 addressed journal transaction ordering for newly allocated blocks, but C2 reveals the fix missed proper resource lifecycle handling in the writepages path where journal handles need different cleanup ordering depending on synchronous vs asynchronous transactions.

cve_description: The IPv6 fragmentation implementation in the Linux kernel through 4.11.1 does not consider that the nexthdr field may be associated with an invalid option, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (out-of-bounds read and BUG) or possibly have unspecified other impact via crafted socket and send system calls.
cause_reason: The original fix added error checking for ip6_find_1stfragopt() in three call sites, but missed two other call sites in xfrm6_mode_ro.c and xfrm6_mode_transport.c where the same function could return negative error values. The follow-up patch adds the same error checking pattern to these overlooked locations that use the same function.

cve_description: In OpenJPEG 2.3.1, there is excessive iteration in the opj_t1_encode_cblks function of openjp2/t1.c. Remote attackers could leverage this vulnerability to cause a denial of service via a crafted bmp file. This issue is similar to CVE-2018-6616.
cause_reason: The initial patch fixed RLE8 data processing in bmp_read_rle8_data() by adding size validation, but the same vulnerability existed in the similar bmp_read_rle4_data() function which processes RLE4 data using nearly identical logic.

cve_description: A memory leak in the nfp_abm_u32_knode_replace() function in drivers/net/ethernet/netronome/nfp/abm/cls.c in the Linux kernel before 5.3.6 allows attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption), aka CID-78beef629fd9. NOTE: This has been argued as not a valid vulnerability. The upstream commit 78beef629fd9 was reverted
cause_reason: C1 routed kzalloc failure through cleanup path that operates on uninitialized match. C2 reverted to return immediately.

cve_description: net-snmp before 5.8.1.pre1 has a double free in usm_free_usmStateReference in snmplib/snmpusm.c via an SNMPv3 GetBulk request. NOTE: this affects net-snmp packages shipped to end users by multiple Linux distributions, but might not affect an upstream release.
cause_reason: The original implementation had inconsistent memory management logic where securityStateRef was manually freed in multiple places, creating double-free scenarios. The fix implements proper reference counting but the follow-up patches reveal the logic was still flawed, requiring removal of explicit free calls that conflicted with the reference counting mechanism.

cve_description: C++ Facebook Thrift servers (using cpp2) would not error upon receiving messages with containers of fields of unknown type. As a result, malicious clients could send short messages which would take a long time for the server to parse, potentially leading to denial of service. This issue affects Facebook Thrift prior to v2019.02.18.00.
cause_reason: The original fix handled invalid skip types in C++ and Python protocols but missed the Go protocol implementation, which still allowed skipping unknown types without validation. The follow-up C2 adds the same invalid type check to the Go protocol's Skip function.

cve_description: FasterXML jackson-databind 2.x before 2.9.10.6 mishandles the interaction between serialization gadgets and typing, related to com.pastdev.httpcomponents.configuration.JndiConfiguration.
cause_reason: The initial patch only blocked one specific gadget class (com.pastdev.httpcomponents) but the follow-up diff shows dozens of additional dangerous classes that needed to be blocked across different libraries and components. The vulnerability existed in multiple code paths through various third-party libraries that weren't covered by the initial narrow fix.

cve_description: A flaw was found in qemu. A host privilege escalation issue was found in the virtio-fs shared file system daemon where a privileged guest user is able to create a device special file in the shared directory and use it to r/w access host devices.
cause_reason: The original C1 patch changed the process namespace setup but missed that the new approach still left security vulnerabilities when handling special files and symlinks. C2 adds comprehensive checks for exceptional file types (non-regular files, directories, symlinks) and race conditions that the original fix overlooked at the same file operation points.

cve_description: A crafted input file could cause a null pointer dereference in jcopy_sample_rows() when processed by libjpeg-turbo.
cause_reason: The original fix addressed merged upsampling cases but missed different SIMD implementation variants (Arm Neon) that use separate non-fancy upsampling routines instead of merged ones. The follow-up had to add platform-specific handling for CPU types that behave differently with the same upsampling operations.

cve_description: The xrdp-sesman service before version 0.9.13.1 can be crashed by connecting over port 3350 and supplying a malicious payload. Once the xrdp-sesman process is dead, an unprivileged attacker on the server could then proceed to start their own imposter sesman service listening on port 3350. This will allow them to capture any user credentials that are submitted to XRDP and approve or reject arbitrary login credentials. For xorgxrdp sessions in particular, this allows an unauthorized user to hijack an existing session. This is a buffer overflow attack, so there may be a risk of arbitrary code execution as well.
cause_reason: The original fix used tui32 (32-bit unsigned) for size variables, but the follow-up patch changes them to int (signed) to properly handle negative values that could bypass the size checks on different platforms or compilers where integer overflow behavior differs.

cve_description: An infinite loop flaw was found in the e1000 NIC emulator of the QEMU. This issue occurs while processing transmits (tx) descriptors in process_tx_desc if various descriptor fields are initialized with invalid values.
